Ensures the investigator/physician site is aware of the requirement of archiving essential documents in accordance with local guidelines and regulations.

• Develops and maintains good working relationship with investigators and study staff, serving as an ambassador to promote Precision high quality and professional image.
• Performs investigational product (IP) inventory, reconciliation and reviews storage and security. Verifies the IP has been dispensed and administered to subjects/patients according to the protocol. Verifies issues or risks associated with blinded or randomized information related to IP. • Applies knowledge of GCP/local regulations and organizational procedures to ensure IP is appropriately (re)labelled, imported and released/returned.
• Performs data review activities, including remote EDC CRF and patient profiles review, query resolution, and assists data management and clinical data quality personnel to resolve data discrepancies.
• Identifies and processes Serious Adverse Events according to the procedures defined by the study team. Also demonstrates a full understanding of the SAE reporting process.
• Identifies site risks and escalates those to Clinical Trial Manager/Project Manager with suggested contingencies. Owns the timely and appropriate resolution of the risk with oversight from project team.
• Prepares for and attends Investigator Meetings and/or sponsor face-to-face meetings. Participates in global clinical monitoring/project staff meetings (inclusive of Sponsor representation, as applicable) and attends clinical training sessions according to the project specific requirements. May prepare or assist in preparation of study-specific presentations/training materials and tools.
• Assists the team managers in the preparation and review of protocols and other study documentation.
• Supports the design and development of CRFs and clinical trial documents as they pertain to clinical monitoring activities (i.e. operating manuals, monitoring guidelines, etc.).
• Assists with review of clinical study reports.
• Functions as a mentor, assisting with the training and developing of new employees and junior monitors.
• Interacts with client, participates in proposal activities, including development and client presentations.
• Initiates payment requests for investigators.
• Travels as necessary according to project needs.

Other required:

Preferred:

jobs.title: Staff / Principal Software Engineer, Detection and Response
jobs.description:
Staff / Principal Software Engineer, Detection and Response

TL;DR You'll build the detection and response capability that catches attackers before they matter - across Lovable's corporate, production, and AI-agent surfaces.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What we're looking for

  • 8+ years in detection engineering, incident response, or threat hunting, with at least 3 at staff/principal level.

  • Strong engineering background - you build detections as code, not as saved searches in a SIEM.

  • Deep experience with cloud telemetry (GCP/AWS/Cloudflare), endpoint EDR, identity logs, and modern SIEM/data-lake stacks (Panther, Elastic, Snowflake/Clickhouse).

  • Battle-tested incident commander who has led real high-severity incidents from first alert to public post-mortem.

  • Adversary-minded: comfortable with MITRE ATT&CK, threat intel, purple-teaming, and red team collaboration.

  • Bonus: detection for LLM/agent abuse, prompt injection at scale, or insider risk in AI-augmented engineering orgs.

What you'll do

  • Build the detection engineering platform - pipelines, detections-as-code, automated triage, and response playbooks.

  • Design and own security incident response process with 24/7 coverage, with a small, high-leverage human and agent team.

  • Lead incidents end-to-end: detection, containment, eradication, post-mortem, and follow-through.

  • Hunt proactively across corporate, production, and AI-agent surfaces - and turn every finding into a durable detection.

  • Define what 'world-class D&R for an AI-native company' looks like, and build it.

Our tech stack

  • Frontend: React and Typescript.

  • Backend: Golang and Rust.

  • Cloud: Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, multiple LLM providers.

  • DevOps & Tooling: GitHub Actions, Grafana, OTEL, infra-as-code (Terraform).

  • Data: Clickhouse, Firestore, Spanner, BigQuery.

And we’re always exploring what’s next!

About your application

Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.
We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

Chargé.e de communication marketing

Chez Lowit, nous avons une ambition : accélérer et massifier la transition énergétique des bâtiments tertiaires.

Face à la hausse des coûts de l'énergie, aux enjeux climatiques et aux évolutions réglementaires, les gestionnaires de patrimoine ont besoin d'outils fiables, mais aussi d'un accompagnement de qualité pour passer à l'action.

C'est pourquoi nous avons développé une plateforme SaaS qui permet de créer le jumeau numérique des bâtiments, de piloter les consommations énergétiques et de construire des trajectoires d'investissement réalistes, chiffrées et adaptées aux enjeux de chaque organisation.

Aujourd'hui, nous accompagnons plusieurs centaines de collectivités et d'entreprises partout en France dans leurs projets de transition énergétique.

Entreprise lyonnaise en forte croissance, nous recherchons des collaborateurs qui souhaitent avoir un impact concret, prendre des responsabilités et contribuer à une aventure collective porteuse de sens.

Vos missions

En lien direct avec le responsable marketing et communication, vous participerez à la mise en œuvre de la stratégie de communication de l'entreprise afin de renforcer sa notoriété, valoriser son offre et engager ses différentes cibles (B2B, secteurs privé et public).

Création de contenus audiovisuels

  • Concevoir, tourner et monter des vidéos : présentations produit, témoignages clients, interviews d'experts, formats courts pour les réseaux sociaux,

  • Réaliser des visuels et supports graphiques en cohérence avec la charte de l'entreprise,

  • Participer à la captation de contenus lors d'événements, de webinaires ou de salons,

  • Adapter les contenus aux différents canaux (sous-titrage, déclinaisons de formats, miniatures).

Rédaction & production de contenus

  • Rédiger des contenus variés : articles de blog, actualités, newsletters, cas clients, communiqués de presse,

  • Adapter le ton et le niveau de langage aux cibles (décideurs, techniciens, collectivités, partenaires),

  • Contribuer à la création de supports marketing : plaquettes, présentations, fiches produit, emailings.

Animation des réseaux sociaux

  • Participation au développement des comptes de l'entreprise (LinkedIn et YouTube),

  • Rédiger et programmer les publications, en adaptant le ton et le format à chaque plateforme,

  • Animer la communauté : veille, interactions, relais des actualités de l'entreprise et de ses collaborateurs,

  • Proposer des formats innovants pour accroître l'engagement (carrousels, vidéos courtes, témoignages, séries thématiques).

Gestion du site web (WordPress)

  • Mettre en ligne et mettre à jour les contenus sur le site : pages, articles, actualités, visuels, vidéos,

  • Veiller à la cohérence éditoriale et graphique ainsi qu'à la qualité des contenus publiés,

  • Appliquer les bonnes pratiques de base (SEO, poids des images, accessibilité, liens).

Événementiel & communication corporate

  • Participer à l'organisation et à la promotion des événements (salons, webinaires, conférences),

  • Contribuer à la communication interne et à la valorisation de la marque employeur,

  • Assurer une veille sur les tendances de communication et les actions des concurrents.

Suivi de performance & amélioration continue

  • Suivre les indicateurs clés (engagement, audience, trafic, taux d'ouverture…) via des outils type LinkedIn Analytics, GA4, outils d'emailing,

  • Réaliser des reportings réguliers et proposer des axes d'optimisation,

  • Participer à l'élaboration et au suivi du calendrier éditorial.

Vos compétences

Vous préparez une formation en communication, marketing, audiovisuel, journalisme ou équivalent (Bac+4 / Bac+5) et souhaitez développer vos compétences sur l'ensemble des leviers de la communication et du marketing.

Vous avez une plume claire et efficace, un bon sens visuel et aimez raconter des histoires, à l'écrit comme en vidéo. Vous savez adapter un message à une cible et à un canal, et transformer un sujet technique en contenu accessible et engageant.

Vous êtes à l'aise avec les réseaux sociaux et avez déjà manipulé des outils de montage vidéo et de création graphique.

Vous êtes rigoureux·se, organisé·e, créatif·ve, curieux·se, et appréciez le travail en équipe : prendre du feedback, itérer rapidement et respecter des délais.

Un plus : compétences en tournage (cadrage, lumière, son), portfolio de réalisations (vidéos, visuels, publications), projets personnels en lien avec la communication, première expérience en communication B2B ou dans le secteur de la transition énergétique.

Compétences clés

  • Excellente qualité rédactionnelle : orthographe, grammaire, style clair, capacité à vulgariser et à adapter son ton,

  • Maîtrise du montage vidéo (CapCut, Premiere Pro, Final Cut, DaVinci Resolve ou équivalent),

  • Compétences audiovisuelles appréciées : tournage, prise de son, vidéo mobile,

  • Connaissance de WordPress et des bases du SEO,

  • Aisance avec les outils de création graphique (Canva, suite Adobe…) et Microsoft Office,

  • Maîtrise des outils IA appliqués à la création de contenus,

  • Rigueur et organisation : gestion de plusieurs projets en parallèle, respect des délais, relecture systématique,

  • Esprit d'équipe : intégrer les retours, travailler avec les équipes marketing, commerciales et experts métiers,

  • Autonomie progressive et force de proposition : capacité à proposer des idées, des formats et des angles de communication.

Staff Engineer / Paris (W/M/X)
Pioneer of online flash sales since 2001 and key player in European e-commerce, Veepee collaborates with over 7,000 brands to offer highly discounted products available for a limited time. Operating across various sectors, including fashion, home, wine, travel or beauty... Veepee achieved a turnover of 3.3 billion euros incl. VAT in 2024 and employs 5,000 staff members across 10 countries.

🎯 Level & Domain

Level:

Staff Engineer is IC4 on our engineering ladder:

  • Has worked as a Senior Developer in at least two product teams. 

  • Turns the tribe’s hardest, ill-framed problems into shipped business value. 

  • Lands in any product fast, de-risks the complex, and raises the bar across teams.

    • The Fastline:

    Each domain has its own Fastline: a small team of Staff Engineers working across all the products of the domain, in a highly agile, commando mode.

    The Fastline is transverse to the domain’s products: it is not attached to one product, but deployed wherever a domain needs senior engineering firepower the most.

    The Fastline takes on three kinds of work:

  • Complex features in existing products: deliver features too risky, cross-cutting or technically hard for a product team to absorb alongside its committed roadmap.

  • Legacy decommissioning: retire legacy systems safely, migrate their capabilities and data, and switch them off for good.

  • IS simplification: reduce the complexity of the tribe’s information system, remove duplication, and make the architecture easier to run and evolve.

    • Fastlines are attached to the Domain Lead, who sets their priorities based on business value, in coordination with the domains’ Lead ITs. Missions are short and outcome-driven: you join a topic, deliver, hand over to the owning product team, and move on to the next one. 


    🎯 TASK

    Strategic & Hard Problems

  • Take on the domain’s most difficult and strategic topics: legacy decommissioning, IS simplification, complex features in existing products.

  • Deliver complex, cross-cutting features inside existing products, working hand in hand with their product teams.

    • Fast Onboarding & Delivery

  • Land in any product or codebase of the domain and become productive in days, not months.

  • Deliver early and often: integrate end to end first, sequence work from most unknown to least worrisome, and show tangible progress quickly.

  • Hand over cleanly to the owning product team: documentation, tests, runbooks and knowledge transfer, so that the team can run what you built.

    • Problem Framing & Business Partnership

  • Take ill-defined, poorly framed problems and turn them into clear, actionable plans.

  • Navigate between tech and business: understand the business stakes, challenge the need with a “how yes” mindset, and propose the simplest solution that delivers the value.

  • Partner with business teams, PMs/POs and Engineering Managers to shape the problem, identify rabbit holes, no-gos and hidden complexity, and agree on scope.

  • Think business value first: explain the value of every technical investment, legacy removal and simplification included.

  • Be the person the business can count on: reliable, transparent on risks, and committed to outcomes.

    • Engineering Excellence & Technical Leadership

  • Write production code: you are hands-on and contribute heavily to the implementation.

  • Raise the bar in the teams you work with: code quality, testing, operability, and AI-first practices.

  • Coach and mentor engineers along the way, and share knowledge across products.

    • Run & Reliability

  • Live by “you build it, you run it”: ship stable, battle-tested software and take ownership of its run until it is handed over.

  • Make migrations and decommissioning safe: rollback plans, monitoring, data reconciliation, progressive switch-over.

  • Step in on critical incidents and complex production problems across the domain when your expertise is needed.

    • AI-First Ways of Working

  • Treat specifications and tests as IP: in an AI era where code is cheap, Veepee’s value moves from code to clear specifications and tests.

  • Use applied AI and prototyping to move faster: understand legacy codebases, generate migrations and tests, explore solutions.

  • Apply a “no roadmap without AI” mindset and spread AI-first practices across the products you work on.


    • 👉 What this role is not
  • Not a manager: you have no direct reports. You lead through expertise, influence and delivery, not hierarchy.

  • Not an ivory-tower architect: you do not draw diagrams and leave. You write code, ship to production and own the outcome.

  • Not attached to a single product: you go wherever the domain needs you most, and you move on once the job is done.

  • Not a spec coder: you do not need a detailed spec to start. A messy, poorly framed problem is your starting point.

jobs.title: GTM & Value Creation Lead
jobs.description:
GTM & Value Creation Lead

About Hexa

Hexa builds and scales software companies alongside entrepreneurs. Since its launch as eFounders, Hexa has helped create companies including Aircall, Spendesk, Front, Swan and Yousign.

Hexa Scale is a small-cap software investment firm deploying a €100 million fund. We take majority stakes in established B2B software companies and work directly with their founders to unlock their next stage of growth. We bring capital, but first and formemost operators who get involved in the daily work to build the fundamentals required to ignite a real Sscaling story: go-to-market, product, hiring and the systems needed.

Hexa Scale

Many software companies have a strong product and loyal customers but have yet to build a repeatable growth engine. Their next phase calls for more than optimising today’s funnel: they need to rethink how they find, win, serve and grow customers as AI changes both customer workflows and commercial execution. They need people who can test what works with their teams and turn the learning into a way of operating.

That is what we do at Hexa Scale. We invest in software companies with roughly €2–10 million in ARR and work alongside their founders after the investment. Our approach is hands-on, with go-to-market at the centre of the acceleration plan?

Mission

We’re looking for a Value Creation Manager with a strong GTM background to join the Hexa Scale team. You will assess growth opportunities and feasibility before an investment decision, then work across our portfolio with founders and their teams to remove growth bottlenecks. Your judgement will help the investment team test whether a company has strong, executable growth potential; your operating work will help turn that potential into results.

This is a GTM-major role: your core craft is building a next-generation go-to-market engine, combining customer insight, commercial execution, data and AI-enabled workflows. You have built or improved commercial motions inside a fast-growing startup, and you are as comfortable with positioning and customer interviews as with sales execution, pricing & process optimization. The remit can become broader as the needs and maturity of each portfolio company change, particularly where product is the best route to more customer value and growth.

You will not be an external advisor producing slides for a management team. You will work with that team, from within the company, establish a useful operating cadence and leave behind a system they can run without you.

What you’ll do

As a preliminary note and as you’ll understand based on the 4 pillars below, the role is in close synch with the investment team. You’ll be a sparing partner, brining both your expert judgement as well as your field working competences to the table. While the role will enable lots of autonomy, you’ll be working in close synch with one or more investment partners, who’re experienced entrepreneurs you’ll learn from and who’ll have the final call on major decisions.

Participate in investment selection

  • Assess growth potential: Work with the deal team before an investment decision to test whether the growth opportunity is substantial, accessible and actionable, rather than relying on an optimistic management plan.

  • Support commercial diligence: support the investment team in interviews of customers and prospects; examine segmentation, win/loss, funnel conversion, sales cycles, retention and expansion, pricing, channels and the capacity of the current team to execute.

  • Underwrite the growth levers: Prioritize potential improvements in GTM, pricing, upmarket sales or distribution. Quantify the starting point, expected impact, costs, timing, dependencies and downside. Separate demonstrated opportunities from assumptions that still need testing.

  • Turn diligence into a plan: Present an evidence-based growth-engineering assessment to the investment team, including what could disprove the thesis and an initial post-close step-by-step execution roadmap. Final investment decisions remain with the partners.

Build a next-generation go-to-market engine

  • Find the constraint: Work with founders and commercial teams to understand where growth stalls, from targeting and lead generation to conversion, onboarding and expansion.

  • Get close to customers: Run interviews, listen to sales calls, examine lost deals and translate what you learn into sharper segmentation, messaging and offers.

  • Run experiments: Lead and co-run tests with teams across outbound, partnerships, demand generation, pricing, AI-assisted prospecting and sales processes. Set a baseline, define what success looks like, measure conversion and unit economics, and stop what doesn’t work, while bringing teams along so the new ways of working stick.

  • Build AI-enabled GTM workflows: Design and test practical workflows for research, targeting, qualification, sales preparation, customer success or expansion using AI tools and agents where appropriate. Measure quality, adoption, cost and human oversight, not just activity or demos.

  • Make the funnel usable: Improve CRM discipline, pipeline visibility, forecasting and the handoffs between marketing, sales and customer success. Automate repeatable work where it improves the customer experience and commercial outcomes.

Execute alongside portfolio teams

  • Connect product and growth: As portfolio needs and maturity vary, partner with product teams to increase customer value and create new growth paths. Explore features such as embedded finance or agentic execution where relevant; validate customer demand, adoption, willingness to pay, implementation costs and margins before treating them as growth levers.

  • Work with founders: Help turn priorities into a weekly cadence, clear owners and decisions grounded in customer and commercial evidence.

  • Build internal capability: Coach or assist in recruiting when needed the people who will own the work long term. Document the useful parts of a playbook without imposing the same answer on every company.

  • Own critical projects: Take responsibility for a defined growth or operating problem, from diagnosis through implementation, rather than handing over a recommendation.

Can include temporary embedding in the company on a full-time basis

Strengthen the Hexa Scale operating model

  • Make our work repeatable: Capture what works across portfolio companies and improve the tools and methods we use to diagnose and accelerate growth.

  • Take on adjacent problems: GTM remains your major, but the most valuable work may extend into product, customer operations, hiring or cross-functional execution depending on the company and its stage of maturity. Know when to take ownership and when to bring in a specialist.

  • Use technology pragmatically: Build and deploy AI-enabled workflows with portfolio teams when they improve GTM outcomes or customer value. Assess reliability, cost and operational fit; do not confuse a demo with an adopted process.

What we’re looking for

Experience

  • Five years or more: Substantial time in a fast-growing startup or scale-up in a hands-on GTM role.

  • Commercial execution: You have personally built, operated or significantly improved a B2B growth engine, ideally in a fast-growing startup. You can explain how you changed the GTM motion, what the numbers showed and what you would do differently.

  • B2B software: You understand sales cycles, conversion, retention, expansion, pricing and the trade-offs involved in scaling a team. Experience in high growth vertical SaaS is a plus.

  • Range: You can work across sales, marketing, customer success and operations without needing a large team or a perfectly defined brief.

  • Working with leaders: Experience alongside founders or senior commercial leaders is a strong plus. French and English fluency are required for this role.

Mindset

  • Autonomous: You can turn an ambiguous problem into a plan, make progress and know when a decision needs to be escalated.

  • Hands-on: You are willing to inspect the CRM, join customer calls, rewrite a sequence and run an experiment yourself.

  • AI-fluent: You already build with AI tools and use them in your daily work, not just in occasional demos. You can show workflows or products you have built, explain what worked and failed, and help teams adopt AI where it changes how they go to market.

  • Commercially sharp: You care about revenue outcomes, not activity for its own sake.

  • Versatile without being superficial: GTM is your major, but you can work on product and wider operating problems when they are the real constraint. You connect new customer value to adoption, pricing, retention and growth.

  • Low ego, high standards: You can challenge a founder’s assumption, listen when you are wrong and earn the trust of the team doing the work.

What we offer

  • Ownership: A role at the centre of Hexa Scale’s work with founders, with responsibility for real operating projects across B2B software companies.

  • Team: Direct collaboration with Hexa Scale partners and access to Hexa’s product, talent, brand and operational expertise.

  • Compensation: A competitive package, including carried interest

  • Benefits: Hexa employee benefits may include a Swile meal card, RTT, a green mobility budget and health insurance.

Recruitment process

Proposed process, to confirm with the Talent team:

  1. Introductory call with Hexa’s Talent team.

  2. Interview with the Hexa Scale team on your GTM experience and operating approach.

  3. Practical case on a real pre-investment growth diligence and portfolio execution problem, followed by a working session.

  4. Conversations with the people you would work with most closely.

  5. Reference checks and offer.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
Heavy- Duty Automation Engineer
jobs.description:
Heavy- Duty Automation Engineer

About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role

As a Heavy-Duty Automation Engineer on Harmattan AI's Launcher team in Lausanne, you will take a clean-sheet, fully autonomous launch system from a blank sheet of paper to live flight tests by simulation, prototype testing and field testing.

Our Launcher team builds the ruggedized, unmanned deployment infrastructure that takes our larger autonomous platforms from storage to flight at a moment's notice. Operating in a fast-paced startup environment within a tight-knit, cross-functional squad, you will own the entire control, automation, and safety architecture end-to-end.

Your work spans defining system specifications, selecting controllers, sensors, and high-speed valves, managing external suppliers, and getting hands-on programming PLCs, wiring prototypes, and tuning closed-loop characteristics and motion controls in the workshop and field.

Responsibilities

  • End-to-End Control & Safety Architecture: Architect, specify, and own the complete control-system work package from initial concept through commissioning and live flight tests by simulation, prototype testing and field testing.

  • PLC & Safety Programming: Develop robust industrial PLC and safety PLC control logic to govern fully autonomous, remotely supervised operations—including self-deployment, automated launch sequences, and autonomous aircraft reloading.

  • High-Acceleration & Precision Control: Select, integrate, and tune motion control systems (controllers, sensors, proportional/high-speed valves) capable of managing both high-precision positioning and extreme launch acceleration.

  • Machine Safety & Risk Assessment: Define safety standards, perform risk assessments, and implement hardware/software interlocks and performance levels for high-energy, unmanned outdoor equipment.

  • Hands-On Commissioning & Field Testing: Wire, calibrate, and commission control hardware on prototype test rigs and deployable systems, troubleshooting and iterating rapidly during live field trials.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with Mechanical, Flight Dynamics, and Operations teams to synchronize mechanical actuation, flight requirements, and autonomous launch sequences.

  • Supplier & Documentation Ownership: Manage external component suppliers and integrators, maintain up-to-date electrical/control schematics, specifications, and commissioning documentation, and drive system reliability.

Candidate Requirements

  • Heavy-Duty Automation & Control Design: Proven experience designing, programming, and commissioning complex, heavy-duty automated machinery from scratch.

  • PLC & Safety Systems Expertise: Deep hands-on experience programming industrial PLCs and safety PLCs (e.g., Siemens, Beckhoff, or equivalent), including machine safety standards, risk assessments, and safety interlock design.

  • Electrical Cabinets & DAQ Architecture: Demonstrated proficiency in layout, wiring, and assembly of industrial control enclosures, alongside real-time data acquisition and test systems (e.g., National Instruments PXI platforms).

  • Hydraulic & Motion Control: Strong practical command of closed-loop characteristics and motion control, high-precision positioning (e.g., automated handling/reloading), and high-acceleration actuation.

  • Hardware Integration & Commissioning: Comfortable getting hands-on with electrical wiring, sensor calibration, valve selection, and field troubleshooting on ruggedized outdoor prototypes.

  • Supplier & Work Package Management: Experience owning automation work packages, sourcing specialized or custom fit-for-purpose control hardware, and managing external vendors.

  • True "Builder" & Startup Mindset: Thrives with high autonomy and end-to-end ownership in a fast-paced environment—equally comfortable architecting control loops, wiring test benches, and supporting live field deployments.

  • Communication & Languages: Fluency in English required (French is a plus), with clear technical documentation skills and full commitment to Harmattan AI’s mission, vision, and growth

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

jobs.title: Junior Business Controller (Data specialist)
jobs.description:
Junior Business Controller (Data specialist)

Do you enjoy working with numbers, analysing data and finding out what is really happening behind the figures? As Junior Business Controller at HG, you will support our Controllers and Group Financial Controller with financial analyses, reporting and increasingly data-driven insights.

At HG, you will work in a compact organisation with an international reach. You will get the opportunity to learn from experienced colleagues, take responsibility early and turn financial and business data into insights that help us make better decisions. We value people who are curious, take initiative and have the energy to turn ideas into action.

About the role

As Junior Business Controller, you will support our Controllers and gradually build your own areas of responsibility. The role combines financial activities with a strong focus on data, analysis and improving management information.

You will:

  • support the Business Controllers with financial analyses, reporting and recurring control activities;

  • own and maintain the data model

  • analyse financial and business data and translate it into useful insights;

  • investigate differences, trends and developments and help explain what is happening behind the numbers;

  • build, review and improve data models used for reporting and analysis;

  • use various tools including Excel and Power BI to make information clearer and easier to use;

  • investigate how data flows from source to report and identify opportunities to improve data quality and reporting;

  • help reduce manual work by finding smarter and more reliable ways of working;

  • contribute to improvements in management information and financial processes;

  • translate questions from colleagues into practical analyses and insights.

An important part of the role is conceptual thinking about data. You understand how information should be structured, see connections between different data points and can think about how a data model can be improved to provide better business insights.

Your development in data

Next to your finance responsibilities, you will grow step by step into the data side of the role, coached by our current Data Specialist. You do not need to master these areas from day one: together we will set up a development path in which you learn to:

  • contribute to HG's Business Intelligence and data strategy, making sure data supports our company goals;

  • design and maintain data models (such as star schemas) and database/Lakehouse structures, so that data is accurate, reliable and accessible;

  • integrate data from different sources and systems in a medallion model (Bronze for raw data, Silver for engineering, Gold for consumption);

  • manage the HG Data Dictionary, data repositories and the underlying data architecture;

  • apply data governance and data quality practices, including audit trails, data privacy requirements and best-practice frameworks such as DAMA;

  • map business processes (BPMN 2.0) and translate business requirements into practical data solutions;

  • work with tools such as SQL, Python (pandas), Power Query, Power Automate and Microsoft Fabric, and over time explore AI techniques;

  • document data models and data processes, and monitor data systems for performance and reliability.

This gives you a strong combination of finance and data expertise, which is becoming increasingly valuable in modern Business Control.

Collaboration & positioning

You will be part of the Finance team and work closely with our Business Controllers. This gives you the opportunity to learn from experienced colleagues while contributing your own analytical and data-driven perspective.

Because HG is a relatively compact organisation, you will have direct contact with colleagues across different disciplines. This means you can quickly see how your analyses and improvements are being used in the business. At the same time, you will work within an international organisation, with colleagues and markets across Europe.

The role is based at our head office in Almere.

HG is a compact, fast-growing and international organization where you can directly see the impact of your work. This requires ownership, initiative and a pragmatic, results-oriented mindset. The team culture is open, pragmatic and focused on results, encouraging you to bring ideas forward, challenge constructively and take responsibility. Everything we do is guided by our three core values: Aim High, Be Brave, Be Connected.


What you bring

We are looking for someone who is analytical, energetic and curious. You enjoy getting to the bottom of a question rather than simply producing a report. You want to understand why the numbers look the way they do and how the underlying data can provide better insights.

You bring:

  • willingness to learn

  • around 3–5 years of relevant work experience, for example as a big 4 auditor, Finance Analyst, Data Analyst or Junior Business Controller;

  • solid knowledge of finance and accounting, preferably gained through an education in Accountancy, Finance & Control, Business Information Management, Data Analytics);

  • experience with or a strong interest in Power BI;

  • strong analytical skills;

  • the ability to think conceptually about data, reporting and data models;

  • a curious and proactive approach to solving problems;

  • the confidence to ask questions and challenge existing ways of working;

  • an energetic mindset and the drive to learn and improve;

  • a genuine eagerness to learn and to keep developing yourself, both in finance and in data;

  • fluent English; knowledge of Dutch is desirable.

  • experience with AI tools, such as Copilot.

    Please note that we do not offer visa or work permit sponsorship for this position. You must therefore hold a valid EU work permit

What we offer

This is a role where you can build a strong foundation in modern Business Control while developing further in data and analytics. You will not only work with existing reports and figures, but also have the opportunity to improve how information is structured, analysed and used.

You can expect:

  • a monthly salary between €4.000 and €5.200 (excluding holiday allowance), depending on your experience.

  • an annual on-target bonus of 10% of your gross annual salary; 

  • full-time employment with 30 days of annual leave; 

  • a pension scheme; 

  • a commuting allowance; 

  • a dynamic and ambitious working environment where initiative and ownership are valued;

  • the opportunity to grow towards a broader Business Controller role as your knowledge, experience and responsibilities develop;

  • structured coaching by our Data Specialist to develop your data skills alongside your finance role;

  • a friendly, welcoming team, with a free shared lunch every Monday and monthly social drinks.

We are HG

HG is a leading European brand in specialist cleaning and maintenance products.

We believe a home should be a place where people can live carefree, with confidence in the products they use to care for the spaces and belongings around them. Our products are developed to do exactly what they promise: deliver effective, reliable and specialist cleaning solutions that help consumers solve real household problems.

HG’s mission is to help people enjoy their homes without worrying about what might go wrong. We do this through high-quality products, specialist expertise, clear advice and a relentless focus on performance.

We are dedicated to delivering superiority, innovation, quality and customer satisfaction. With a strong presence across Europe and beyond, we are continuously investing to make an even bigger impact.

HG does what it promises.

Our colleague Ilse de Groot, Corporate Recruiter, will be happy to answer any questions. You can contact her at

Would you like to apply for the junior business controller position at HG? You can apply directly by uploading your CV. We aim to respond within 5 working days.

Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager Creative
Software Engineer (Python & Cloud)
jobs.description:
Software Engineer (Python & Cloud)

Build the software behind large-scale battery storage

Solar and wind power are not always available when we need electricity. Large-scale battery storage helps by storing electricity when supply is abundant and releasing it when demand rises. This keeps the grid flexible and reduces reliance on fossil fuels.

But how do you connect a battery site of hundreds of megawatts to a central IT platform? And how do you build software that is ready for the projects still to come? As a Software Engineer at GIGA Storage, these are the challenges you will work on.

About GIGA Storage

Founded in 2018, we are an international scale-up growing across the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany. Our purpose, ‘Unlock every Green Watt’, is about making the energy system better and more affordable for future generations. We aim to have 1.5 to 2 GW of battery power operational by 2030. At 2 GW, that is theoretically enough peak power to supply more than a million homes simultaneously.

We pioneer at a scale where many solutions are still being developed. We take ownership, share knowledge and make decisions together. Rapid growth also calls for adaptability: priorities shift and not everything is defined in advance.

Your role

You develop and grow our Giga platform. You build software in Python, working with technologies including SQL, Terraform, Grafana and data processing. You do not need to know everything already: you enjoy learning beyond your own specialism.

What will you work on? When a new battery site goes live, data on capacity, performance and equipment status needs to flow reliably into our platform. You build the software and integrations that make this happen. At the same time, you strengthen the foundations: fewer manual steps, better-documented code and reusable solutions for future sites. We work by the principle ‘you build it, you run it’. You can propose tools and improvements; important technical decisions are made together with the team and our IT Lead.

What will you do?

  • Build software. Develop and maintain Python services and integrations for new battery sites.

  • Make data reliable. Build and improve data pipelines, quality checks and monitoring.

  • Work smarter. Automate repeatable tasks and improve documentation, standards and maintainability, using AI tools where useful.

  • Own what you build. Test, deploy and support your software, and discuss technical improvements with the team.

  • Add knowledge, creativity and fun to the IT team.

What do you bring?

  • Higher professional education (HBO) level of thinking and working, and at least four years of relevant software development experience.

  • Python experience; one year may be sufficient if you have also programmed in other languages.

  • Experience with at least one cloud platform: GCP, AWS or Azure.

  • Interest in data engineering and DevOps; Terraform, SQL and CI/CD knowledge is a plus.

  • A broad technical mindset, ownership and a willingness to automate, document and share knowledge.

  • Good English communication skills and availability to work from our Amsterdam office at least three days a week.

Energy-sector experience and Dutch language skills are not required.

Why join GIGA Storage?

  • Visible impact. Your software helps bring new battery sites into operation.

  • Technical variety. Combine software, data and cloud while broadening your skills.

  • Room to contribute. Help automate our platform and prepare it for the next stage of growth.

  • Build together. Join five international IT colleagues in our new Buitenveldert office, close to Amsterdam Zuid.

What do we offer?

  • A competitive salary plus holiday allowance (8%)

  • A fixed year-end bonus (7-9%) and performance-related bonus (max 10%).

  • 28 days of annual leave for full-time employment

  • A pension plan.

  • A €750 annual learning budget, laptop, phone allowance and e-bike scheme.

  • Hybrid working: at least three days a week in our Amsterdam office; choose home or office for the remaining days.

  • Healthy lunches and occasional fun activities

Ready to build with us?

Want to develop software that matters while working on the energy transition? Apply through our website. We look forward to meeting you!

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Fulfilment
jobs.description:
Senior Product Manager, Fulfilment

About Nivoda

Nivoda is the operating system for the global jewellery industry. Our marketplace connects jewellers with suppliers of diamonds, gemstones, melee and finished jewellery in 70+ countries, with more than $300M in annual transactions and a $350B industry still waiting to be modernised. We are scaling fast, and we are only getting started.

Our Mission

For decades, the diamond trade has been slow, opaque and inefficient: hard to find stock, hard to trust prices, hard to know when anything will arrive. Nivoda exists to change that. We give businesses of every size, in every location, the same access to inventory, the same transparent pricing and the same reliable delivery as the biggest players in the industry.

The Fulfilment & Express Team

The Fulfilment & Express team is where Nivoda's promise to buyers is kept. We own how an order travels from supplier to jeweller: the delivery date we promise, the hubs that hold and check stock, the carriers that move it, and the returns and quality checks that protect every purchase. We are a remote-first team of product, engineering, design and QA who work closely with Operations, Customer Support, Sales and Supplier Experience. We are low on hierarchy and high on ownership, and we like solving problems where software meets the physical world.

About the Role

As our Senior Product Manager for Fulfilment & Express, you will own how Nivoda orders get from supplier to jeweller: accurately promised, reliably tracked and delivered fast. You will set the strategy and roadmap for a complex, operationally heavy product area that spans diamonds, gemstones, melee and finished jewellery, with physical hubs, carriers and suppliers behind every screen. Your work decides whether a jeweller trusts Nivoda with their next order, so this is a role with real commercial impact and plenty of room to lead.

What would YOU be doing?

  • Setting the fulfilment strategy for the next 2 to 4 quarters, making trade-offs explicit, including what we are choosing not to do and why

  • Owning the roadmap and the numbers: running quarterly planning, sizing opportunities and setting targets for delivery-as-promised, delivery date accuracy and delivery speed

  • Making our Promised Delivery Dates trustworthy by rolling out SLA-based, dynamic delivery dates across every category and route, and shaping how they are used for delay communications and, in time, shown to buyers

  • Scaling Express, our hub-based fast-delivery offer, including hub workflows (receiving, inventory and RFID put/pick, QC and dispatch), ready-to-wear jewellery, consignment flows and speed options such as same-day pickup

  • Owning jewellery returns and on-platform QC, from the manufacturer through to the hub, including hallmarking and consignment returns to suppliers

  • Improving the delivery experience through carrier and rate/transit integrations, consolidation, last-mile cost and efficiency, and clear order visibility for buyers

  • Translating hub operations, carrier behaviour, customs and supplier handling into clear product requirements, designing for the exceptions as much as the happy path

  • Turning support tickets, delay breaches, supplier performance data and customer feedback into prioritised problems, then deciding what to build, buy or fix operationally

  • Partnering daily with Engineering and Design, and closely with Operations, Customer Support, Account Management, Sales, Supplier Experience and Fintech so delivery, credit and payments feel like one journey for the buyer

  • Writing sharp PRDs and decision records, and reporting progress openly through our weekly updates

  • Mentoring other product managers and designers on working in operationally complex domains

What do we need from YOU?

  • 5 to 8 years in product management, including experience owning a complex product area end to end

  • Experience in fulfilment, logistics, supply chain or other operations-heavy products. You are comfortable where software meets warehouses, carriers, SLAs and customs

  • Strong systems thinking: you can map a multi-party process, find where promises break, and design for failure modes, delays and edge cases

  • Data fluency: you define the right metrics, query and interrogate data yourself (Snowflake, Mixpanel or similar) and use it to decide what to build next

  • Sound prioritisation and commercial judgement: you weigh impact, effort and risk honestly, say no clearly, and can explain the return on a fulfilment investment to leadership

  • Excellent cross-functional leadership: you build trust with engineers, operators and commercial teams, and influence without authority across time zones

  • Clear written communication: concise PRDs, roadmaps and updates that make decisions easy

  • Customer and operator empathy, and high agency: you spend time with jewellers, support teams and hub operators, you take ownership, and you follow things through to the outcome

Nice to have

  • Jewellery, diamond or luxury goods experience

  • Marketplace or B2B commerce experience, ideally two-sided with supply and demand constraints

  • Experience with carrier or shipping APIs, rate and transit tools, 3PL integrations, inventory systems or RFID

  • Experience building predictive or SLA-based estimates, such as delivery dates or ETAs

  • Experience with cross-border shipping, customs, duties or compliance (for example hallmarking and HS codes)

Our culture and what we offer

Nivoda is collaborative, high-growth and built on empowerment. You will have real ownership from day one, a team that wants you to succeed, and the chance to keep learning as the company scales. We are remote-first with flexible hours, and we trust you to do your best work your way.

Our current benefits

  • ⏰ Flexible working hours and a vibrant company culture

  • 🏡 Remote work

  • 🩺 Private health insurance

  • 📚 Opportunities for growth and learning

  • 💳 Flexible compensation card (meals, transport, childcare)

  • 🌴 Unlimited holiday allowance

  • 🚀 The chance to join during an exponential expansion phase

Equal opportunity

Nivoda is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team, and we welcome applications from everyone. Even if you do not meet 100% of our musts, do not let it stop you. If this role excites you, we would love to hear from you.

Full-Time Netherlands, UK, USA

jobs.title: Data Engineer - Senior Consultant
jobs.description:
Data Engineer - Senior Consultant

Ready to build data platforms, not just pipelines?

At Opencast, we believe great data engineering is about more than moving and transforming data. It's about creating reliable, scalable foundations that help organisations make better decisions and deliver better services.

You’ll tackle complex engineering challenges across integration, migration, modelling and platform design, working with Microsoft Fabric, Azure and modern data technologies. We value engineering craft, thoughtful problem-solving and building solutions that are simple, robust and built to last.

Our data engineering capability is growing, and you'll help guide its direction through mentoring, recruitment and technical leadership, as well as your client work. If you want to shape both the solutions and capability around them, this could be the role for you.

 

The role

  

Opencast data engineers help organisations transform how they manage, use and learn from data. The work ranges from building modern lakehouse and warehouse platforms in Microsoft Fabric to modernising legacy environments, migrating complex workloads and improving the quality, governance and reliability of critical data services.  

 

This role offers the opportunity to work across the full data lifecycle, combining platform design, engineering, integration and optimisation. Expect to work with structured, semi-structured and unstructured data, building batch and near real-time data pipelines that underpin critical business and public services.  

 

You'll collaborate with architects, analysts, software engineers and client teams to solve complex challenges and influence technical direction. The role also offers opportunities to contribute beyond delivery through mentoring, recruitment, community building and helping to define engineering standards and best practice as our capability continues to grow. 

 
 

Requirements

 
This role involves weekly on-site work, and you’ll be required to travel regularly to client locations across the UK. We’re looking for people who value in-person collaboration, enjoy building strong relationships, and are passionate about delivering solutions that make a real difference for our clients.
 
Due to the nature of this role, you must either hold active Security Check (SC) clearance or be eligible and willing to undergo the clearance process. 
 
SC clearance is granted in line with UK Government security vetting requirements. Typically, applicants must have UK citizenship and have lived continuously in the UK for at least the past five years, with no single absence exceeding 28 consecutive days. Nationality and immigration status may also be considered as part of the vetting process. We are unable to progress applications from candidates who do not meet these requirements.
 
If you are unsure whether you meet the eligibility criteria, we encourage you to review the guidance or discuss this with us before applying.
 

We are recruiting for multiple positions, with opportunities available immediately and in the coming months. If you are interested in joining Opencast, we encourage you to apply. 

 
 

Essential experience

 
 
We're looking for engineers who enjoy solving complex technical problems and care about building solutions that are robust, scalable and built to last. 
 
Experience in the following areas is important: 
  • Microsoft Fabric and Azure data services, including lakehouse, warehouse, notebooks and pipeline capabilities.

  • Data modelling and dimensional modelling techniques such as Kimball. 
  • ETL/ELT development and large-scale data integration.  
  • PySpark, Spark SQL and modern transformation techniques.  
  • Advanced SQL and relational databases including SQL Server, PostgreSQL and Oracle. 
  • Integrating structured, semi-structured and unstructured data sources.  
  • Migration and modernisation of legacy platforms such as Oracle, SQL Server/SSIS or Synapse.  
  • Power BI semantic models, curated datasets and supporting analytics platforms. 
  • Data quality, governance, metadata management and lineage. 
  • Data security, classification and access control approaches. 
  • Automated testing, validation, reconciliation testing and performance optimisation. 
  • DataOps, CI/CD and version control practices.  
  • Agile delivery environments. 
 

Essential consulting skills

 
 

Our clients look to us for more than technical delivery. 

 

Success in this role comes from being able to navigate ambiguity, solve difficult problems and help clients make confident technical decisions. The strongest consultants combine technical expertise with curiosity, pragmatism and a collaborative mindset. 

 

You'll thrive in this role if you enjoy: 

  • Solving complex engineering challenges and exploring different approaches to finding the right solution.  

  • Influencing technical direction through expertise, evidence and constructive challenge.  

  • Working closely with technical and non-technical stakeholders to understand underlying problems rather than simply implement requirements.  

  • Balancing engineering quality, governance, security and reliability with business outcomes.  

  • Sharing knowledge, mentoring others and helping raise engineering standards.  

  • Building trusted relationships with clients and acting as a technical advisor.  

  • Keeping pace with emerging technologies and evaluating new approaches where they can add value.  

  • Contributing to a growing engineering capability while remaining close to delivery and technology. 

 

 

Salary

 
£61,000 - £70,000 per annum.
 

What we offer


A competitive package including a 7% employer pension contribution, share options, and a discretionary bonus. You’ll also benefit from 25 days’ holiday and access to 3 annual “life happens” days to support unexpected situations.  We provide wellbeing support, ongoing professional development, volunteering opportunities, and the chance to be part of a genuinely supportive team.

Where you’ll work


This role requires regular on-site attendance at our HQ, hub offices, and client sites, as well as the ability to work from home. Applicants must be able to travel to offices and client sites across the UK as part of their normal working arrangements, as travel is essential for fulfilling the responsibilities of the role.

We include you


We welcome candidates from all identities, attributes, ways of thinking and backgrounds to thrive in a career at Opencast. Our aim is for the diversity of our people to be reflected in the solutions we deliver, to help create a fairer society for all.   

Interview


Interviews will be conducted via Microsoft Teams. We’re happy to make adjustments to support your needs.

jobs.description:
Staff Backend Engineer - Ledger Platform

Staff Backend Engineer - Ledger Platform

Hybrid in London, UK

We’re looking for a Staff Backend Engineer to join the Ledger Platform team.

You'll design and build iwoca's new ledger platform – the distributed system that records every movement of money, starting with the business credit card and moving on to loans.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The Ledger Platform team is rebuilding all of iwoca’s ledgers as one platform, starting with the ledger for the business credit card. Every card payment, loan repayment, and payout will end up there. Finance, Accounting, and Capital Markets rely on that record, so it has to be right every time.

The team is small – a principal engineer who leads it, another staff engineer, another engineer, and you. It works closely with the product teams that build on its ledgers, and with Finance.

The role

You'll lead projects from design to production, and decide with product what the team builds and how. With the principal engineer, you’ll set the platform’s technical direction, from service boundaries to the APIs and event streams other teams build on. Most of the platform is still to be built, and you’ll own part of it yourself. It’s a hands-on individual contributor role with high ownership and no line management.

Every payment a small business makes with iwoca crosses several services and network hops before it reaches the ledger, and any of them can fail. You'll build services that record each one exactly once, with no single point of failure, safe timeouts and retries, and graceful degradation when a dependency is down. When something breaks in production, you'll fix it so it doesn't break again.

You’ll learn iwoca’s financial products in depth, so you can challenge requirements and explain technical trade-offs to Finance. When the answer isn’t obvious, you’ll scope and prototype, and use domain modelling to find the simple design behind a complicated problem. You’ll influence which parts of a problem need solving now, which can wait, and which aren’t worth solving at all.

Live project examples:

  • New ledgers. Building the ledgers for Flexi-Loan and iwocaPay.

  • Account migration. Moving existing loan accounts onto the new ledgers with zero downtime and no data lost.

  • Credit card ledger. Building new features for the credit card ledger, from real-time card holds to daily interest and monthly statements.

  • Reconciliation and journals. Reconciling the ledger with banks, payment providers, and the card scheme, and producing the accounting journals Finance relies on.

  • Funding facilities. Recording how loans move between iwoca’s funding facilities.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Distributed systems. You’ve built and run fault-tolerant services in production, and handled the hard parts: durable communication between services, idempotency, transactional correctness, and partial failure.

  • Backend engineering. You have deep expertise in at least one object-oriented language. You’ve written and run backend services in it.

  • Databases. You’ve worked in depth with relational databases, ideally PostgreSQL, and solved data integrity, concurrency, and performance problems in them.

  • Ownership. You’ve led large projects across several engineers or teams, end to end, and helped other engineers grow through design and code reviews.

  • Testing. You’ve tested for edge cases and failures as carefully as you designed for them.

  • AI leverage. You’ve built agentic workflows, or used AI to scale your engineering output beyond what you could deliver alone, at work or in your own projects. You judge when to use it and when not to, and you check its output before it reaches production.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

  • Financial systems. You’ve built ledgers, billing, or payment systems, including the audit trails and reconciliation that prove they’re correct.

  • High volume. You’ve worked at a company where the volume of data or transactions shaped how you designed systems.

  • Migrations. You’ve moved live systems and data onto a new platform with zero downtime.

  • Python. You’ve used Python in production, with a web framework such as Django, FastAPI, or Flask. It’s the language the team works in.

  • Data tooling. You’ve built pipelines with Snowflake and dbt, or similar, that turn ledger data into reports for Finance.

  • Messaging. You’ve built asynchronous messaging with queues or topics, such as Kafka.

The salary

We expect to pay from £110,000 to £140,000 for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

Useful links:

  • iwoca benefits & policies

  • Interview welcome pack (TAP)


Compensation: £110K – £140K

Nos solutions sont installées dans plus de 600 services médicaux et utilisées par plus de 15 000 professionnels de santé en France et en Europe.

Mission principale

Au sein de l'équipe Administration & Finance France, le/la Chargé(e) de facturation maintenance assure la gestion et le suivi de la facturation des contrats de maintenance et des prestations associées.

  • Identifier les nouveaux formats et les opportunités permettant d'améliorer la visibilité et les performances des comptes.

VOTRE RYTHME DE PRODUCTION

Vous évoluerez sur un portefeuille de 7 à 8 clients, avec un rythme pouvant aller jusqu'à :

4 stories par semaine et par client.

1 carrousel par semaine et par client.

4 Reels diffusés par semaine et par client.

Vous travaillerez en coordination avec nos équipes de création de contenu, qui vous accompagneront dans la production des contenus photo et vidéo.

Vous serez accompagné·e à votre arrivée par notre directrice des opérations et une Social Media Manager senior. L'objectif : vous permettre de prendre progressivement vos marques et de gérer votre portefeuille en autonomie.

LE PROFIL QUE NOUS RECHERCHONS

Nous recherchons une personne ayant déjà une première expérience professionnelle en Social Media Management.

Une expérience dans la restauration, la gastronomie, l'hôtellerie ou l'Hospitality sera particulièrement appréciée.

Deux critères sont indispensables pour ce poste :

1. Vous avez déjà géré plusieurs comptes Social Media simultanément.

Vous avez une expérience concrète de la gestion de plusieurs comptes clients en parallèle. Vous savez jongler entre différents univers, respecter des calendriers éditoriaux et adapter votre communication à chaque marque.

Une première expérience en agence ou dans un environnement multi-clients est particulièrement pertinente.

2. Vous avez un véritable intérêt pour la gastronomie et les univers haut de gamme.

Restaurants, chefs, belles maisons, hôtels, expériences gastronomiques… Ces univers vous attirent sincèrement.

Vous n'avez pas nécessairement besoin d'y avoir travaillé, mais vous devez avoir envie de les découvrir, d'en comprendre les codes et de savoir les mettre en valeur.

Au-delà de ces deux indispensables, vous êtes une personne qui :

  • Possède un véritable œil esthétique et une forte sensibilité à l'image.

  • Maîtrise les codes d'Instagram et des formats courts.

  • Aime créer des contenus visuels et monter des vidéos.

  • Possède de bonnes capacités rédactionnelles et une orthographe irréprochable.

  • Est curieuse, créative et attentive aux tendances Social Media.

  • Fait preuve de rigueur, d'organisation et d'une grande attention aux détails.

  • Sait gérer plusieurs projets et priorités en simultané.

  • Est autonome, réactive et apprécie le travail en équipe.

  • A envie d'apprendre, de progresser et de s'investir dans une agence ambitieuse.

CE QUE NOUS VOUS PROPOSONS

Une rémunération adaptée à votre expérience :

Profil junior : 27 000 à 28 000 € brut annuel fixe complété par une rémunération variable pouvant atteindre 1 000 € brut annuel.

Profil expérimenté : rémunération pouvant atteindre 35 000 € brut annuel fixe selon l'expérience et le niveau d'autonomie.

VOS AVANTAGES

Télétravail : prime mensuelle de 50 € brut.

Transports : prise en charge de 50 % de l'abonnement aux transports en commun, y compris en télétravail.

Noël : bons cadeaux offerts.

Croissance de l'agence : mise en place en cours d'une prime complémentaire liée au développement de Culinary Agency.

Matériel professionnel : iPhone et ordinateur fournis.

ORGANISATION DU TRAVAIL

Localisation : Lyon

Nous fonctionnons actuellement sans bureaux fixes. Nous privilégions le télétravail et les sessions de travail en cafés avec le reste de l'équipe, organisées régulièrement. Des bureaux sont envisagés dans les prochains mois.

Horaires habituels : 9h30 – 18h30, avec une certaine flexibilité selon les besoins des clients.

Organisation libre entre télétravail et sessions de travail avec l'équipe.

Déplacements :

Environ un déplacement par trimestre en Île-de-France.

Quelques déplacements ponctuels en région selon les besoins des clients.

NOTRE PROCESSUS DE RECRUTEMENT

Nous souhaitons prendre le temps de rencontrer les candidats et d'évaluer concrètement leur sensibilité créative, leur compréhension des réseaux sociaux et leur capacité à gérer plusieurs comptes clients.

Notre processus se déroule en quatre étapes :

1. Entretien de préqualification en visioconférence

Un premier échange pour faire connaissance, comprendre votre parcours et vous présenter Culinary Agency.

2. Étude de cas / mise en situation

Si le premier échange est concluant, nous vous proposons un exercice pratique pour mieux comprendre votre approche créative et votre manière de travailler.

3. Prise de références professionnelles

Nous souhaitons échanger avec des personnes ayant déjà travaillé avec vous.

4. Entretien final avec le CEO fondateur

Un dernier échange pour approfondir votre candidature et vous permettre de découvrir la vision et les ambitions de l'agence.

POURQUOI REJOINDRE CULINARY AGENCY ?

Rejoindre Culinary Agency, c'est intégrer une agence en pleine croissance, spécialisée dans des univers passionnants, où l'image, la créativité et le sens du détail occupent une place centrale.

Vous travaillerez sur des projets variés, auprès de restaurants, chefs, hôtels et marques, avec la possibilité de développer votre expertise en Social Media Management dans l'univers de la gastronomie et de l'Hospitality.

Vous aimez les beaux contenus, les belles histoires et les univers qui ont une véritable identité ?

Vous avez envie de rejoindre une équipe ambitieuse et de participer activement au développement d'une agence en pleine expansion ?

Nous serions ravis de découvrir votre profil !

Alongside our platform, we provide application development and support services to a select group of key enterprise accounts. They rely on us not just for their infrastructure, but also to build, evolve, and support the applications that run on it. Because we run the platform as well as the code, we own the whole chain from development to production.

The role

You will join a small cross-functional team working on a large, multi-site enterprise application, building re-usable frontend components and complete user-facing features, implementing tools, integrating external services and creating features and functionality that are used across multiple sites and audiences.  You will work closely with our backend and infrastructure engineers, our platform team, and the clients themselves. 


Your work will include:

  • Building features: designing and developing modern, maintainable frontends for client applications, mainly in React and TypeScript.
  • Owning quality: keeping client codebases healthy, secure, accessible, and performant over the long term, not just shipping and moving on.
  • Working with clients: turning requirements into practical solutions, giving estimates, and explaining technical trade-offs clearly to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Deploying: taking your work from development to production on the Divio platform and on AWS.
  • Supporting: helping with technical questions and issues on the applications we maintain, as part of a weekly support rotation.
  • Shaping how we work: contributing to frontend standards, reviews and tooling across the project, and having a say in our quarterly objectives.

Requirements

Who we're looking for

We're looking for someone who:

You will develop regional customer communications and campaigns while building a repeatable advocacy engine across customer stories, references, third-party reviews, speakers, and other strategic opportunities. You will work closely with Customer Success, Sales, Product Marketing, Product, and the broader Marketing team to turn customer needs and business priorities into useful, measurable programs.

What you will do

Confirm speakers early enough to include them in event promotions, landing pages, emails, and social campaigns, and manage briefing, preparation, logistics, approvals, and follow-up.

Program operations and measurement

  • Experience building customer journeys and programs across adoption, engagement, retention, renewal, expansion, or advocacy.

jobs.title: Talent Acquisition Partner - Tech (f/m/d)
jobs.description:
Talent Acquisition Partner - Tech (f/m/d)

This is for the person who's looking for their next growth challenge in recruiting. You can close a hard search, you know how to talk to candidates who aren't looking, and your current role has started to feel a little too comfortable.

At eleQtron, you can still help write our next chapter and decide how we get there. We build quantum computers, with about 130 people across Hamburg and Siegen. Most of the people we need are physicists, engineers and software specialists who are sought-after talent. We’re still shaping how eleQtron finds them, how it tells them why they should join, and how we evolve our approach to hiring. That's the job you can define.



What you'll do

  • You'll sit inside our technical teams as their talent partner. You'll learn how each team works, where it’s strong and where the gaps are. You'll shape the brief and the bar with the hiring manager, pushing back where you have to.

  • You'll run our hardest searches yourself, from mapping the market to closing the offer and helping people relocate. Most of those hires will be people you found rather than people who applied.

  • With the team, you'll work out why a strong scientist or engineer should join eleQtron, and you'll make sure the people we want to hire hear it, through universities, conferences and research networks as well as the usual (and unusual) channels.

  • You'll build the way we hire: structured interviews, scorecards and debriefs that every technical team uses, with the data to show whether they work. You'll coach our hiring managers and interviewers to that standard.

  • You'll have the freedom  to be creative in how you source, and to use AI for the research and admin, so your time goes on judgement and on conversations with people.

This is for you if

  • You've outgrown your current role and want to build something.

  • You start things without waiting to be asked, and you finish them.

  • You move with urgency when the picture is still unclear.

  • You'd rather shape an employer brand than inherit one.

  • Hard technical searches interest you more than easy ones.

You don't need to have built a recruiting function before. If you have, that helps, but what matters more is your appetite to continually improve and push us forward. If you haven't, we care more that take initiative without being asked and you to and seen it through, taking the time to learn what worked, or not.

What’s worth knowing

Our People team has a lot to deliver. You'll build while you hire, and the hiring won't wait for the building to finish. Some searches will take months, and the people you talk to will be comparing us with big tech and research labs. You'll also spend regular time at both our Hamburg and Siegen sites.

So this probably isn't for you if:

  • You want a settled process to run.

  • You're happy with the way things are and want to keep them that way.

  • You'd rather someone else decided how hiring should work.

  • You need a clear path with little ambiguity.

What you'll bring

  • You've recruited scarce technical specialists from start to finish: finding people who weren't looking, persuading them, and closing them through offer and relocation. You’re used to be rejected or ghosted.

  • You've worked closely with technical leaders and shaped what they hire for, with evidence to back your view.

  • You can show us something you initiated that had a meaningful impact without waiting to be asked to do it.

  • You're fluent in English. German is a plus.

It helps if you've also built a hiring process, worked on an employer brand or coached other people to a standard. If you haven't, curiosity, a growth mindset and pace go a long way.

How we hire

  • A 40-minute call with our Head of People & Culture to find out more about you, your background and experiences, and how this could fit into the role at eleQtron.

  • A 45-60 min light hands-on case study with a short fictional brief that you’ll work through with the hiring manager.

  • A practical exercise: 60 minutes with one of our technical hiring managers, to work through a live role-intake and search calibration meeting to assess how you apply your knowledge, work directly with a key stakeholder and how you get to the most effective outcome together.

**You can also have an informal coffee with the other team members at any point.

Please note, that this job will remain online until the 19th of December for new applications at which point it will be closed.

If you've read this far and you're already thinking about what you'd change first, we'd like to hear from you!
