Abhängig von Ihrem gewünschten Arbeitsort können Sie am Standort München oder Berlin angestellt werden. Sie erhalten, falls Sie nicht schon dort wohnen, auch eine hochwertige Firmenwohnung.

Wir suchen im Rahmen einer unbefristeten Festanstellung direkt bei unserem Kunden eine/n:

Projektleiter SF-Bau (m/w/d) | 80.000 - 120.000 € brutto/Jahr - besondere Work-Life-Balance

  • Gesamtleitung eines zugewiesenen Bauvorhabens über alle Teilprozesse und Arbeitsschritte im Hinblick auf Termine, Kosten und Qualität

Corporate Fitness-Room und bundesweitem Gesundheitscoaching, Job-Rad, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, ein attraktives Mitarbeiterempfehlungsprogramm und vieles mehr.

About us

CMR is first and foremost a team of people, passionate about the construction industry and changing the way project controls is provided.

We are a progressive and dynamic consultancy offering tailored project controls services across a range of industries.

Our Purpose (Why we exist): Inspiring new ways to help shape our construction industry.

  • Support the Project Management and Commercial Teams in the effective identification, assessment and management of project risks.

Financial Crime Analyst

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

We’re looking for a Financial Crime Analyst

If you’re curious, analytical and enjoy getting into the details, this could be the role for you. You’ll dive into suspicious activity, help protect small businesses from fraud and financial crime, and play a key part in keeping our processes sharp and secure. We're looking for candidates based in either London or Leeds.

The role
iwoca's Financial Crime Analysts protect our customers and our business from fraud. You'll become an expert in how fraudsters target small businesses and card products, helping our business credit card grow safely while keeping the experience smooth for genuine customers.

You'll investigate suspicious applications, accounts and card activity, owning the process from first alert to final decision. Working closely with our Credit Cards and Operations teams, you'll spot new fraud patterns early to help strengthen our controls. From time to time, you'll also support our core lending business with fraud cases on our Flexi-Loan, giving you a wider view of financial crime across iwoca.

Your mission will be:

  • Investigating cases flagged as a potential fraud or AML risk. Including CIFAS flags, facial biometric anomalies, device based anomalies, signs of document tampering and more.

  • Screening PEP, sanction and adverse media matches.

  • Taking ownership of customer verification on a case by case basis and deciding what information is required to reduce the risk of fraud and money laundering.

  • Monitoring account activity and transactions, investigating anything unusual and raising unusual activity where needed.

  • Identifying opportunities to improve our processes and implement changes which will make us more efficient

  • Working closely with our Account Managers, Credit Analyst and Broker teams to maintain our high fraud prevention standards while ensuring a fast and slick service.

The requirements

We look for people who are smart, humble, motivated and who are always looking to improve.

Ideally, you’ll have:

  • Good knowledge of fraud and financial crime

  • Brilliant communication skills and experience delivering constructive and candid feedback

  • A confident and enthusiastic attitude that works well in a regularly changing and fast-paced environment

  • A pragmatic, risk-based approach to case investigation

Whilst we welcome applications from all qualified candidates, please note that this particular position does not offer visa sponsorship. Candidates must be eligible to work in the UK independently.

The salary

Our base salary range in Leeds is £30,000 - £35,000 and our base salary range in London is £35,000 - £40,000. We want to pay all of our employees fairly, so that’s why we regularly benchmark salaries based on market rates and to recognise your increasing value to our business.

Senior Technical Program Manager

About Volta

Volta is the category-defining, fully vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform – from capital to clusters to software, under a founder-led enterprise. Our mission is The Utility of Compute™: AI infrastructure as dependable and available as electricity, for every organization that needs it. Launched with a $10B strategic partnership with one of the leading frontier AI labs, a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, and a $5B AI Infrastructure Fund, Volta is building the infrastructure layer of the AI era from the ground up. We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds.

About The Role

As a Technical Program Manager for GPU and Data Center Deployments, you will own end-to-end program delivery for bringing data center infrastructure and AI clusters online. You will operate in a highly ambiguous environment, coordinating across construction, infrastructure, networking, systems engineering, procurement, and operations — driving execution from planning through operational handoff.

 

This is an ownership role. You will be expected to move programs forward with incomplete information, surface and resolve gaps before they become blockers, and hold multiple workstreams accountable across time zones and organizational boundaries. The best candidates bring deep experience at the intersection of data center construction handover and AI/GPU hardware deployment. You know how construction sequences impact infrastructure readiness, how ICT and CDU work intersect, and how to drive multi-threaded bring-up programs spanning hardware, networking, power, and cooling.

 

What You'll Do

Program Delivery & Execution

  • Own end-to-end delivery of GPU cluster activations and data center infrastructure programs, from initial strategic planning through operational handoff.

  • Drive multi-threaded bring-up programs spanning hardware, networking, power, and cooling — owning plans, dependencies, and critical paths.

  • Coordinate cross-functional teams responsible for construction, infrastructure, network, hardware, ICT, commissioning, and operations, including vendor and contractor partners.

  • Anticipate downstream impacts of technical sequencing decisions on capacity, schedule, and cluster performance; identify and resolve blockers before they surface.

  • Manage and hold accountable vendors, integration contractors, and third-party service providers across the full deployment lifecycle.

  • Partner with engineering to improve cluster turn-up reliability, repeatability, and automation — reducing time-to-serve for new capacity.

  • Support network operations and end-to-end physical and logical bring-up, including on-site deployment, rack cabling, and coordination with engineering teams.

  • Maintain momentum through changing requirements, tight timelines, and cross-time-zone execution.

Stakeholder & Executive Communication

  • Influence senior executive and c-suite strategic approaches.

  • Deliver crisp executive-level program status briefings covering schedule health, risks, key decisions, and escalation paths across a broad portfolio of concurrent programs.

  • Translate complex technical requirements — from highly detailed customer RFPs, integration specs, and architecture documents — into actionable plans for engineering, finance, and marketing stakeholders.

  • Serve as the primary cross-functional point of contact between engineering, operations, customers, and leadership; code-switch fluently between deeply technical and business-facing audiences.

  • Interface with chip and hardware providers to derisk onboarding to new platforms across compute, networking, and cooling stacks.

  • Facilitate alignment across stakeholders at all levels — from network engineers to C-suite — with confidence, clarity, and no ego.

Program Infrastructure & Process

  • Build and operationalize program mechanisms — roadmaps, milestones, risk registers, RACI matrices, decision logs, and deployment runbooks — that make delivery predictable at scale.

  • Establish and maintain a single source of truth for all active programs using tools such as Smartsheet, Confluence, Jira, and Notion.

  • Identify bottlenecks and systemic gaps, then drive durable fixes across tooling, process, and partner interfaces.

  • Develop scalable playbooks and governance frameworks that create accountability without creating overhead as Volta's deployment footprint grows rapidly.

  • Champion automation and digital workflows to eliminate manual effort across the program lifecycle.

 

What You'll Bring

Required

  • 5+ years of experience delivering complex data center physical infrastructure programs or large-scale GPU/AI cluster deployments in fast-moving environments.

  • Demonstrated experience bridging construction handover and cluster deployment — candidates who are network-only or construction-only will not be a fit.

  • Hands-on GPU deployment experience, including:

  • GPU cluster deployment and activation (NVIDIA infrastructure preferred)

  • Full-stack secure AI factory deployment across compute, networking, storage, and security layers

  • Ability to read, interpret, and operationalize highly technical customer and vendor specifications

  • Strong understanding of AI/GPU infrastructure including power density, cooling (CDU/DLC), networking, and deployment sequencing.

  • Familiarity with how construction, low-voltage, and commissioning activities affect deployment readiness and sequencing.

  • Proven ability to lead through influence — you don't own the execution teams, but you are accountable for delivery outcomes.

  • Proven ability to manage vendor and contractor relationships, including understanding schedule and reputational risks.

  • Ability to develop and present executive-level program status, risk summaries, and key decisions to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder alignment skills — able to ensure teams at all levels understand priorities and dependencies.

  • Relentlessly resourceful: you thrive in ambiguous, fast-paced environments and drive execution beyond your defined scope without being directed to do so.

  • Startup or scale-up experience alongside enterprise pedigree is strongly preferred — candidates who have operated at both ends of that spectrum understand the range of environments this role will demand.

Preferred

  • Degree in a hard science, engineering, or a demonstrated track record of technical depth in comparable work.

  • Experience delivering programs across multiple concurrent sites or regions, including EMEA, with staggered milestones.

  • Experience managing long-lead procurement processes and hardware supply chain constraints that affect deployment timelines.

  • Background at a Fortune 100 infrastructure company (NVIDIA, Intel, Dell, Cisco, Verizon, AT&T) combined with startup or scale-up experience.

  • Experience managing BPO or contract labor pools during large-scale hardware deployment phases.

  • Automation-first mindset with experience identifying and implementing process improvements at scale.

  • DCD, PMP, CDCPM, CDCMP, CDCP, or comparable certification(s).

 

Who You Are

  • You have operated in highly ambiguous, fast-moving environments and know how to prioritize ruthlessly without losing sight of the long-term picture.

  • You have startup instincts — you fill gaps, take initiative, and drive execution beyond your defined scope before anyone asks you to.

  • You have enough confidence to hold the room and none of the ego that slows the work down.

  • You are not a 9-to-5 operator. Global infrastructure programs run across time zones — you know how to chase the sun.

  • You have built the business case, secured buy-in from technical stakeholders, and presented to executive decision-makers who pushed back hard.

  • You bring a strong execution mindset with the ability to balance speed, quality, and risk — and you make decisions with data, not assumptions.

  • You are interested in and thoughtful about the impact of AI infrastructure on the world.

What We Offer

Senior Internal Automation Engineer

About Volta

Volta is the category-defining, fully vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform – from capital to clusters to software, under a founder-led enterprise. Our mission is The Utility of Compute™: AI infrastructure as dependable and available as electricity, for every organization that needs it. Launched with a $10B strategic partnership with one of the leading frontier AI labs, a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, and a $5B AI Infrastructure Fund, Volta is building the infrastructure layer of the AI era from the ground up. We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds.

About the role

Volta builds and operates large scale GPU compute infrastructure for frontier AI customers. Growing this fast produces a long tail of manual internal work: invoices retyped into banking portals, expense reports chased by hand, spreadsheets reconciled every month, accounts provisioned ticket by ticket. Each task is small. Together they cost the company real time, and they multiply with every new sit and every new hire.

This role removes that work permanently. You sit with the person who owns a process, understand what it actually does, then build the integration that runs it against banking and accounting systems, Microsoft Graph / Office, Slack, Jira and Confluence, and the HR and identity stack. Most of the answer is well built API code with sound authentication, error handling, escalation, audibility and observability. Some of it uses models, for classification, extraction, or matching, where that is the right tool rather than the fashionable one. Knowing the difference is a large part of the job.

Much of this work lands inside the financial reporting path, and Volta is building toward SOX compliance alongside its existing ISO 27001 and SOC 2 obligations. An automation that touches invoices, payments, or reconciliation becomes part of the control environment the moment it goes live. That sets the bar: changes are reviewed, tested, and traceable, access is least privilege and segregated, every run leaves an audit trail an external auditor can follow, and nobody moves code into production by hand. You build to that standard from the first commit rather than retrofitting it under deadline.

Regulation shapes the work in a second way. Volta is headquartered in the UK and operates across the EU, so anything you build with AI in it sits under the EU AI Act as well as UK and EU data protection law. Automation that touches hiring, performance, or other employment decisions carries the heaviest obligations, and the line between a helpful classifier and a regulated decision system is easy to cross without noticing. You are expected to recognize where that line runs, keep a person in the loop where the law requires one, document what you deploy, and bring Legal and Security in early rather than after the build.

You sit inside Corporate IT at a fast-growing AI-forward company, which owns the tooling, accounts, and API access you build on, and which gives you engineers next to you for design discussion and code review rather than leaving you to mark your own homework. Security Engineering advises on access and compliance. The first internal customer is the accounting and finance team. After that the scope is the whole company: finance, IT, People, delivery, product, and the engineering teams for their own internal overhead. Very little here is customer facing. Initially, you are the only person doing this work full time, so you prioritize hard, ship small, and build things that keep running without you next to them.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Automate finance operations first: ingest received invoices into banking and bookkeeping systems, classify and match them, and close the loop on the exceptions

  • Work directly with process owners across finance, IT, People, and delivery: take a described workflow and turn it into a specified, testable automation

  • Work as part of Corporate IT: review their changes, have yours reviewed, and keep automation aligned with how the underlying systems are administered

  • Build and run integrations against internal systems, including Microsoft Graph, Slack, Atlassian, banking platforms, and HR and identity tooling

  • Own authentication and credentials for those integrations: OAuth flows, service principals, scoped tokens, secret rotation

  • Build every finance touching automation to withstand audit: version controlled and peer reviewed changes, automated deployment with no manual production edits, least privilege service identities, segregation of duties preserved rather than automated away, and retained evidence of what ran, when, and on whose authority

  • Work with Finance and Security Engineering on control design, so an automation replaces a manual control with a stronger automated one instead of quietly removing it

  • Apply models where they earn their place, for document extraction, classification, or matching, and use conventional code everywhere else. Keep a human decision point where a control requires one

  • Build agentic automations where a single scripted path will not hold: an agent that picks up a case, calls the tools it needs across Microsoft Graph, Slack, Atlassian and the finance stack, and stops at a human approval gate before anything with money or access impact. You define the tool surface, the permitted scope, and the blast radius, rather than handing a model a broad credential and watching what happens.

  • Keep AI use inside its regulatory boundaries: automatically classify use cases correctly under the

  • EU AI Act, apply transparency and human oversight where required, document deployed systems, and escalate anything touching employment decisions to Legal before it is built

  • Instrument what you build so failures surface immediately and the state of any run is visible without reading logs

  • Maintain what you deploy, including the unglamorous part where an upstream API changes and the process still has to run on Monday

  • Set the patterns, repositories, and review practices that keep internal automation maintainable and auditable as more of it accumulates

  • Push back when a process should be simplified or deleted instead of automated

What You Bring

  • Production software development held to the standard of an engineering team, not scripting attached to an operational role

  • Fluency across more than one software ecosystem. Internal systems arrive in whatever language, runtime, and SDK their vendor picked, and you are expected to work in what the problem needs rather than bending every problem toward one stack. Python and Go come up often here, neither is a requirement

  • Deep practical work with third party APIs: pagination, rate limits, idempotency, retries, webhooks, and how an integration behaves when the far end is having a bad day

  • Real command of authentication mechanisms, including OAuth 2.0, OIDC, service accounts, and API key and secret management

  • Disciplined engineering practice that produces an audit trail as a by-product: source control, code review, automated testing, controlled deployment, and clear separation between who builds a change and who releases it

  • Hands on experience building with LLMs, including tool use and structured extraction, plus the judgment to recognize when a model is the wrong answer

  • Hands on work with agentic patterns: tool and function calling, MCP or equivalent tool interfaces, state and retry handling across multi step runs, and testing agent behavior against realistic cases before it touches a production system.

  • Working awareness of the rules governing AI and automated decision making in a workplace context, at the level of knowing which use cases need legal review before a line of code is written

  • Ability to sit with a subject matter expert, understand a business process well enough to implement it correctly, and translate it without needing them to specify the solution

  • A track record of building reliable, secure, auditable systems rather than demos that work once

  • Comfort as the only engineer on a problem: choosing what to build next and owning the outcome

Nice to Have

  • Delivering AI systems under the EU AI Act: risk classification, technical documentation, transparency and human oversight obligations

  • Building or operating systems in SOX scope: IT general controls, change management, segregation of duties, and producing evidence for external audit

  • Finance systems experience: accounts payable, expense management, bank reconciliation, ERP integration

Sr. Account Executive, Retail Media

Help retailers turn shopper intent into a growing media business

Constructor helps e-commerce businesses connect shoppers with the products they want through AI-powered search and product discovery.

We’re looking for an experienced Retail Media sales professional to help grow our business across EMEA. You’ll work with retailers to understand their monetisation ambitions, build compelling business cases and sell technology that helps them develop and scale their Retail Media offering.

This is a hands-on commercial role—not a campaign-operations position. You’ll combine deep industry knowledge with enterprise sales discipline, working alongside Account Managers and the wider Sales team to turn qualified opportunities into lasting customer partnerships.

What you’ll do

Own Retail Media opportunities from discovery to close

  • Identify and qualify opportunities with retailers looking to launch, improve or scale their Retail Media business.

  • Lead consultative discovery with Retail Media, e-commerce, commercial and technology stakeholders.

  • Build opportunity strategies with clear decision processes, executive engagement and agreed next steps.

  • Lead proposals, negotiations and commercial agreements in partnership with the relevant account owner.

  • Maintain a credible pipeline and an evidence-based forecast.

Build business cases that stand up to scrutiny

  • Understand each retailer’s commercial model, advertiser demand, inventory and operational readiness.

  • Translate those inputs into clear monetisation scenarios, with transparent assumptions and measurable success criteria.

  • Explain how sponsored products, display formats and relevant integration approaches can support the retailer’s objectives.

  • Work with technical and product specialists to define demonstrations, proof plans and realistic delivery expectations.

  • Help customers evaluate revenue potential alongside shopper relevance, customer experience and operational requirements.

Navigate a complex buying group

  • Build relationships with senior Retail Media, digital, commercial and technology leaders.

  • Help stakeholders align around the opportunity, investment and path to launch.

  • Understand the relationship between retailer economics and the needs of brands, sellers and agencies.

  • Address commercial and organisational blockers rather than treating every challenge as a product gap.

Make the wider commercial team stronger

  • Partner with Account Managers on Retail Media expansion opportunities within existing customer relationships.

  • Support Sales colleagues where Retail Media is part of a broader customer proposition.

  • Share discovery frameworks, objection handling, business-case approaches and lessons from live deals.

  • Help develop a repeatable Retail Media sales motion across EMEA.

  • Ensure closed opportunities move into delivery with clear commitments, ownership and success criteria.

Bring market insight into the business

  • Share customer feedback, competitive insights and emerging buying requirements with Product and leadership.

  • Represent Constructor in relevant customer conversations and industry events.

  • Help sharpen our positioning through practical knowledge of what retailers need to build a sustainable media business.

What you’ll bring

  • A proven track record selling Retail Media, commerce media or closely related advertising technology.

  • Experience managing complex enterprise sales cycles, from discovery and business case through negotiation and close.

  • A strong understanding of retailer monetisation and the relationships between retailers, brands, sellers and agencies.

  • The ability to discuss media performance, measurement and incrementality—and distinguish credible evidence from assumptions.

  • Confidence engaging senior commercial and technical stakeholders.

  • Strong commercial judgment, pipeline discipline and forecasting skills.

  • An ability to make complex technology and business models easy to understand.

  • A collaborative approach: you can lead a specialist sales motion while respecting the broader customer relationship.

  • Professional fluency in English.

Your experience may come from a Retail Media platform, an adtech provider or a retailer’s media business. What matters is your ability to combine industry expertise with demonstrated commercial delivery.

It would be a bonus if you have

  • Experience selling retailer-facing technology that enables Retail Media networks.

  • Experience with sponsored products, onsite display, auctions or mediation.

  • Familiarity with enterprise e-commerce and product discovery.

  • Experience working across several EMEA markets.

  • Relationships within the European Retail Media ecosystem.

  • Additional European language skills.

Patient Support Coordinator

Behind every patient enquiry is a person who deserves to feel heard, understood and supported.

At Montu UK, we are improving access to cannabis-based medicines for patients living with a range of chronic and often debilitating conditions. Many of our patients have spent years navigating the healthcare system, and our Patient Support team plays a vital role in ensuring their experience with us is as seamless and supportive as possible.

We are looking for a compassionate, proactive and resilient Patient Support Coordinator who understands what excellent patient care looks like and thrives in a fast-paced environment.

This is a busy, telephone-based role where no two conversations are the same. You will need to balance empathy and understanding with efficiency, accountability and the ability to work towards performance targets, ensuring every patient receives the quality of service they deserve.

What is the job?

As a Patient Support Coordinator, you will be one of the first points of contact for our patients, supporting them throughout their treatment journey.

From answering questions about appointments and prescriptions to managing more complex or sensitive enquiries, you will take ownership of patient queries, provide reassurance and work collaboratively with our Clinical and Pharmacy teams to find appropriate solutions.

You will be working in a high-volume environment, handling approximately 450 inbound and outbound calls per week, alongside emails and live chats.

What will you be doing?

  • Providing an exceptional patient experience across telephone, email and live chat.

  • Supporting patients with treatment enquiries, appointments, prescriptions and general queries.

  • Managing approximately 450 inbound and outbound calls per week.

  • Handling sensitive and challenging conversations with empathy, patience and professionalism.

  • Taking ownership of patient enquiries and proactively finding appropriate solutions.

  • Working towards individual and team KPIs and service targets without compromising the quality of patient care.

  • Collaborating with our Clinical and Pharmacy teams to ensure a seamless patient journey.

  • Recognising and escalating clinical concerns to the appropriate teams.

  • Maintaining accurate patient records and adhering to GDPR requirements.

What do you need?

We are looking for someone who genuinely enjoys helping people, takes pride in delivering excellent service and has the resilience to manage a busy and demanding workload.

Ideally, you will have:

  • A minimum of two years of experience in a customer service or patient-facing role.

  • Confidence in managing difficult or sensitive conversations.

  • Excellent communication and active listening skills.

  • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.

  • Empathy, patience and emotional resilience.

  • Experience working towards KPIs and performance targets.

  • Confidence navigating multiple IT systems.

Montu UK is a leading digital health company specialising in cannabis-based medicines (CBPM), dedicated to improving patient access to safe and effective treatments. jobs.description:
Senior SecOps Engineer

About Equativ & Security team

Equativ is an independent ad tech company. Our programmatic advertising platform runs at high scale, with production running entirely on Google Cloud Platform. Equativ is building its ISMS toward ISO 27001 certification, targeted by the end of 2027.


The role

You run day-to-day security operations for a full-cloud company as a senior engineer in the SecOps team, reporting to the SecOps Manager. You bring technical proposals to the SecOps Manager; the IT & Security lead approves the SecOps roadmap. 

You back up the SecOps Manager on technical topics and during incidents. 

You are also the link between SecOps and the other teams, mainly R&D, Platform Engineering and IT. You keep them in sync on security priorities, changes and incidents. You train them on secure practices and on the security tooling they use, so they can own security in their own areas.

Most of your time goes into building and running things yourself. You write the Terraform, the detections and the automation.


Responsibilities

  • GCP guardrails and posture as code: definition, organization policies, IAM and service-account hygiene, VPC Service Controls, Cloud Armor, KMS and Secret Manager; run our CSPM (Wiz); take controls from monitoring to enforcement with a rollback plan; deliver controls in Terraform and CI/CD policy checks with Platform Engineering.

  • Detection and incident response: own log pipelines (Cloud Logging, audit logs, Workspace, Okta, CrowdStrike), build detections end to end (log onboarding, SIEM use cases, validation) and manage alert quality, automating triage and enrichment; lead security incidents from triage to root cause and post-mortem, including GCP forensics; maintain playbooks and run tabletop exercises.

  • Vulnerability and attack-surface management: cloud, containers (GKE, Artifact Registry), dependencies and external surface; prioritize findings on exploitability and real exposure; run the technical side of external pentests (scoping, challenging findings, retest) and drive remediation with owning teams and track SLAs.

  • Secure development: threat-model new services with R&D; embed SAST, SCA, secret and container scanning and supply-chain controls in the SDLC; be the security contact for each R&D team.

  • Assurance: produce technical evidence for ISO 27001 audits; answer the technical part of customer security questionnaires and RFPs, including non-standard requests; assess the security of third-party vendors.

  • FinOps: know the cost of the security tooling you deploy, flag cost drifts early and work with Procurement on cost estimates when selecting security vendors.


    • Must-have profile

  • 7+ years in security engineering or SecOps, including 3+ years securing production on a public cloud — GCP strongly preferred, AWS/Azure transferable.

  • Deep GCP security knowledge: IAM model, org policies, VPC-SC, SCC, logging, GKE security.

  • Hands-on experience with cloud-native security platforms such as Google SecOps (Chronicle), Security Command Center (SCC) and Wiz (or similar CNAPPs).

  • Hands-on incident response experience, including leading incidents and cloud forensics.

  • Detection engineering with a SIEM and log pipelines at scale.

  • Infrastructure as code (Terraform) and scripting.

  • Clear written and spoken English and French; able to explain risk to engineers and to customers.

  • Skills in project management

  • Proactive, bring forward proposals and make recommendations


    • Nice to have

  • Kubernetes / GKE hardening and runtime security.

  • Experience in ad tech or other high-throughput, latency-sensitive platforms.

  • Exposure to ISO 27001 or SOC 2 audits from the operations side.

  • Identity and endpoint stack: Okta, Google Workspace, CrowdStrike.

  • Certifications: GCP Professional Cloud Security Engineer

We are proud to be rated 4.7 on Trustpilot, based on 60,000 reviews. Our culture puts customer satisfaction at the core of what we do (more about our culture here).

 

[OUR JOURNEY] Founded in 2016 and launched in 2017 by Alexandre and Steve, Qonto has grown to 1,700 Qontoers serving over 750,000 customers across 8 European countries. We have been profitable since 2023, and we are just getting started.

 

[OUR BELIEFS] We hire for skills and potential. With 80+ nationalities, 45% women, and 56% of women in our leadership team, diversity isn't a program; It's who we are. We've built a discrimination-free hiring process because the best teams are built on merit.

 

[AI AT QONTO] AI is deeply embedded in how we work (here) - Every Qontoer gets unlimited access to the best AI tools. We want people who experiment without waiting for permission, push AI beyond the obvious, know when to trust it, and when to question it.

Join our Finance Crime team as an Anti-Financial Crime Officer, specialized in sanctions, PEP analysis and adverse media investigations. You'll screen and resolve complex alerts, make accept/refuse calls on transaction screening, and help sharpen our second-line sanctions controls, under the guidance of Martina, our Lead AFC Sanctions & Investigations.

 

➡️ What you'll do

  • Screen and investigate alerts: you review sanctions, PEP and adverse media matches from our screening tool (ComplyAdvantage), assess real exposure, and document your conclusions with a full audit trail.

  • Decide on transaction screening alerts: you accept or refuse alerts within defined criteria, and escalate the ambiguous or high-risk ones to senior leads.

  • Keep files audit-ready: you maintain detailed PEP and sanctions case documentation, and handle asset-freezing and homonymy declarations to the DGT.

  • Be the reference for your markets: you're the go-to sanctions & investigations contact for your assigned markets, keeping procedures, evidence packs and decision rationales ready for internal and external review.

  • Work across teams and improve how we work: you partner with AML, Fraud, SEPA and Open Banking colleagues to resolve complex cases, and you spot gaps worth fixing in our processes and screening-tool calibration.

➡️ What we're looking for

  • Sanctions & PEP expertise: you have at least 1-2 years (including apprenticeship) in compliance, sanctions regimes, PEP frameworks and adverse media standards, and you keep that knowledge current as regulations evolve.

  • Hands-on screening experience: you're comfortable screening and investigating alerts in tools like ComplyAdvantage, backed by a foundational understanding of AML/CFT.

  • Documentation discipline: you build clear, complete, audit-ready case files and control narratives that hold up under real scrutiny.

  • A cross-functional instinct: you work well with AML, Fraud, SEPA and Open Banking teams, and you're quick to spot and propose fixes for process or calibration gaps.

  • Market and language coverage: you're comfortable being the point of contact for one or more European markets, with the language coverage that requires.

➡️ What we can offer you

  • Real ownership: you make daily accept/refuse decisions on sanctions and PEP cases that genuinely matter, not just paperwork.

  • A seat across Risk & Compliance: you work closely with AML, Fraud, SEPA and Open Banking teams across Qonto's European markets.

  • A voice in how we improve: beyond casework, you contribute to process and screening-tool calibration projects.

➡️ Your future manager

jobs.description:
Enterprise Account Executive Benelux (Remote Benelux)

The AI orchestration of your wildest imagination.

n8n is the open workflow orchestration platform built for the new era of AI. We give technical teams the freedom of code with the speed of no-code, so they can automate faster, smarter, and without limits. Backed by a fiercely inventive community and 500+ builder-approved integrations, we’re changing the way people bring systems together and scale ideas for impact.

Since our founding in 2019, we’ve grown into a diverse team of over 260 - working across Europe and the US, connected by a shared builder spirit and with our centre of gravity in Berlin. Along the way, we’ve:

  • Cultivated a community of more than 650,000 active developers and builders

  • Earned 190K+ GitHub stars, making us one of the world’s Top 40 most popular projects

  • Backed by top investors, from Sequoia’s first German seed to our SAP's recent strategic investment - bringing us to a $5.2bn valuation


That’s the company we’ve built. Now we’d love to see what you can build. If you’re applying, try n8n out - whether you’re technical or not - and share a screenshot of your first workflow with us. The easiest place to start is here: app.n8n.cloud/register.

We’re in a defining moment of an incredible journey. Come and build with us.

🎯 Your main goal will be to win and grow Enterprise customers by becoming the trusted partner of technical teams and their leaders.

As an Enterprise Account Executive covering Benelux (Belgium and the Netherlands), you will own a territory of larger organisations and drive complex deals from first conversation to signature:

GENERATE NEW-LOGO PIPELINE

  • Build and execute account plans for named Enterprise accounts with 1,001 to 5,000 employees.

  • Run outbound campaigns that open doors with CTOs, engineering leaders and platform teams.

  • Turn community adoption and inbound signals into structured enterprise opportunities.

LEAD COMPLEX, MULTI-STAKEHOLDER DEALS

  • Run deep discovery, quantify business impact and build a business case with your champions.

  • Map decision makers across engineering, IT, security and procurement and keep every thread alive.

  • Partner with Solutions Engineers on technical evaluations and proofs of concept.

CLOSE AND EXPAND

  • Own the sales cycle through security, legal and procurement reviews, typically over two to four months.

  • Negotiate with confidence and keep clear commercial control of next steps.

  • Hand over to Customer Success and plan expansion across teams and use cases.

REQUIREMENTS

Must-haves

  • 🏢 Enterprise SaaS sales: You have sold B2B SaaS into organisations of roughly 1,001 to 5,000 employees and can explain customer size, deal complexity and cycle length.

  • 🧑‍💻 Technical buyers: You have sold to developers, engineers, CTOs, CIOs and DevOps or platform teams, and you explain complex products without leaning on a Solutions Engineer.

  • 🧩 Complex deals: You have run multi-stakeholder cycles of two to four months and closed meaningful deals in organisations of 1,001 to 5,000 employees.

  • 🎯 New-logo hunter: You generate your own pipeline through outbound and win new customers rather than living off expansion or inbound.

  • 📈 Track record: You have consistently hit or exceeded quota over the past two to three years.

  • 🧭 Structured selling: You use a structured methodology (MEDDPICC or similar is a plus) and navigate technical evaluations, procurement, legal and security reviews.

  • 📍 Location: You are based in Belgium or the Netherlands, and you already have the right to work there.

Nice-to-haves

  • 🛠️ Technical product background: You have sold developer tools, cloud infrastructure, data, AI or automation platforms.

  • 🚀 Startup or open-source exposure: You have worked at an open-source, product-led or Series A to C company.

  • 🤝 Technical network: You already know engineering and IT leaders in your territory.

Why join us?

You will win Enterprise customers with a product technical teams already love, and you will help define how we sell to larger organisations as the segment takes shape. You will work closely with Solutions Engineers, Customer Success, Partnerships and Product, so your voice carries weight. n8n is growing at an exceptional pace, backed by a vibrant community and a remote-first culture built on autonomy, experimentation and high talent density. Apply now and help us bring AI-powered automation to the world’s most ambitious companies.

n8n is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

We can sponsor visas to Germany; for any other country, you need to have existing right to work.

Our company language is English.

You care about diversity and inclusion? We do too! Check out our Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging initiatives at n8n (https://www.notion.so/n8n/Diversity-inclusion-and-belonging-n8n-c1bec2fff536422d868b1a438d990e35).

Location disclaimer: If you see multiple job postings for the same role, it is most likely because we're hiring remotely for this role and posting in different locations to make sure every potential candidate can see the role. Please apply to the location you're the most likely to work from in the future.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation 💸 – We offer fair and attractive pay.

  • Ownership 💪 – Our core value is to “empower others,” and we mean it—you’ll get a slice of n8n with equity.

  • Work/life balance 🏖️ – We work hard but ensure you have time to recharge:

    • Europe: 30 days of vacation, plus public holidays wherever you are.

    • US: 20 vacation days, 8 sick days, plus public holidays wherever you are.

  • Health & wellness 🩺 –

    • Europe: We provide benefits according to local country norms.*

    • US: Multiple low-premium, low-deductible medical plans with coverage for individuals and families—plus a no-cost premium HDHP option with a pre-seeded HSA—along with dental and vision coverage.

  • Future planning 💰 –

    • Europe: We provide pension contributions according to local country norms.*

    • US: 401(k) retirement plan with a 4% employer match.

  • Financial security 🛡️ –

    • Europe: We provide benefits according to local country norms.*

    • US: Company-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance, plus life insurance to support you and your loved ones.

  • Career growth 📈 – We hire rising stars who grow with us! You’ll get €1K (or equivalent) per year to spend on courses, books, events, or coaching to level up your skills.

  • A passionate team 🤩 – We love our product, and we prove it with regular hackathons where we see who can build the coolest thing with it!

  • Remote-first 🌏 – Our team works remotely across Europe, with regular off-sites for team bonding. Some roles, like sales in the US, are hybrid—please check the job description.

  • Giving back 🤝 – We're big fans of open source, and you'll get $100 per month to support projects you care about.

  • Transparency 🙏 – We all know what everyone’s working on, how the company is doing—the whole shebang.

*Country and/or State specific details provided in your employment agreement.

jobs.title: Security Engineer, Offensive Security
jobs.description:
Security Engineer, Offensive Security

Role Description

As anÂ Offensive Security Engineer within Dropbox Security, you will investigate how attackers could compromise our products and infrastructure, including AI-enabled applications and agentic systems. You will help identify meaningful attack paths and improve the controls intended to prevent, detect or contain them.

This is a hands-on offensive security and threat research role with broad scope and meaningful impact. You will contribute to investigations and multi-phase red team exercises, help prioritize work based on risk, develop attack techniques, and build tooling and automation that expand the reach of our security testing. You will apply practical AI security knowledge alongside broader offensive security skills across applications, cloud infrastructure, and identity systems. Working closely with experienced researchers and partners across Product Security, Detection & Response, Threat Intelligence, Privacy, and engineering, you will help translate technical findings into clear business risk, recommend practical improvements, and validate their effectiveness through retesting. Sound judgment, clear communication, responsible execution, and ownership of your work are essential to the role. You will contribute to the Red Teamâs tools, research methods, and testing practices while developing your own areas of expertise, investigating emerging technologies, and helping advance Dropboxâs offensive security capabilities. You will have opportunities to deepen your skills, publish research, take on increasingly complex projects, and see your work influence security decisions across Dropbox.

Our Engineering Career Framework is viewable by anyone outside the company and describes whatâs expected for our engineers at each of our career levels. Check out our blog post on this topic and more here.

Responsibilities

  • Plan and execute offensive security assessments by defining objectives, scope, rules of engagement, and safeguards, adapting your approach as new evidence emerges.
  • Investigate unfamiliar applications, infrastructure, APIs, and trust boundaries to identify and trace meaningful attack paths.
  • Develop and safely demonstrate exploits and attack chains that clearly establish potential impact to Dropbox.
  • Build and improve offensive security tools, agents, automation, and testing harnesses, ensuring results are reliable, repeatable, and appropriately validated.
  • Assess security risks across AI-enabled applications, agents, tool integrations, and supporting infrastructure, including the responsible use of AI-assisted research techniques.
  • Partner with security, privacy, legal, and engineering teams to communicate risk, strengthen prevention and detection capabilities, address root causes, and verify improvements through retesting.

Many teams at Dropbox run Services with on-call rotations, which entails being available for calls during both core and non-core business hours. If a team has an on-call rotation, all engineers on the team are expected to participate in the rotation as part of their employment. Applicants are encouraged to ask for more details of the rotations to which the applicant is applying.

Requirements

  • 5+ years in offensive security, vulnerability research, red teaming or closely related security engineering, or equivalent demonstrated capability.
  • A track record of independently leading complex investigations or engagements and discovering and exploiting non-trivial vulnerabilities.
  • Understanding of application security, authentication and authorisation, cloud infrastructure, APIs and software supply chains, with deep practical expertise in one or more areas and the ability to trace attack paths across systems and trust boundaries.
  • Hands-on experience attacking or evaluating LLMs, AI agents, ML systems, AI-enabled applications, or agentic architectures.
  • Familiarity with security risks in AI-enabled applications, agents and tool integrations, and the ability to investigate unfamiliar technologies.
  • Ability to write code to build or adapt offensive tools and automation, and to read and investigate unfamiliar production codebases.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience developing novel attacks, repeatable security evaluations or testing frameworks for AI-enabled systems, or building and validating AI-assisted offensive research capabilities.

At ClickUp, we're building the future of work: the first truly converged AI workspace unifying tasks, docs, chat, calendar, and enterprise search, all supercharged by context-driven AI. We're hiring a Senior Technical Account Manager who has already done this job at a SaaS company: someone who has led complex implementations and owned enterprise relationships for the long haul, and who builds with AI rather than just using it.

TAMs at ClickUp are the long-term technical and strategic partner for a portfolio of enterprise customers. This isn't a relationship-only CSM role, and it's not an implementation role where you get buried in requests and lose the account strategy. You'll discover the business problem, build and implement the right solution, drive adoption, and prove the business impact, staying with your customers from first rollout through renewal and expansion, turning delivered value into a credible growth story.

Own your customers for the long term

  • Be the strategic and technical owner of a portfolio of enterprise accounts, from first rollout through renewal and expansion.

AlphaSense is the AI platform redefining market intelligence and workflow orchestration, trusted by thousands of leading organizations to drive faster, more confident decisions in business and finance. The platform combines domain-specific AI with a vast content universe of over 500 million premium business documents — including equity research, earnings calls, expert interviews, filings, news, and internal proprietary content. With AI solutions like Generative Search, Generative Grid, and Deep Research, AlphaSense delivers the clarity and depth professionals need to navigate complexity and obtain accurate, real-time information quickly. For more information, visit www.alpha-sense.com. Come join us.

About the Team

AlphaSense's Product team stands at the forefront of innovation, developing AI-powered solutions that enable professionals to make smarter, faster, and more informed decisions. Our team, a diverse and global collective of operators, craftspeople, innovators, and visionaries, shares a passion for solving complex problems and delivering exceptional user experiences.

If you're passionate about creating industry-leading tools that shape the future of business intelligence, we'd love to meet you.

We are seeking a senior, deeply technical product leader to own Search and Curated Experiences AlphaSense. Search is the front door to a corpus of hundreds of millions of business documents, and the relevance, ranking, document-type coverage, filtering, and performance you own sit underneath every product surface. Curated Experiences define how AlphaSense’s content, functionality, and intelligence show up in pre-built experiences that act as a launchpad for our customers’ research - everything from company profiles and industry profiles, to monitoring and beyond.

This is a leadership role, not a feature role. You will set the search strategy, own the metrics, and be the person the organization turns to drive impact with both Search and Curated Experiences. You will lead a small team, including a domain-expert for Curated Experiences. We expect you to own these programs end to end, with the judgment, drive, and initiative to take them all the way.

What You'll Do

  • Own both Search and Curated Experiences: Relevance, ranking, query understanding, document-type coverage, filters, latency, and reliability across every surface that depends on search are your ownership areas, alongside adoption and engagement of company profiles and future new curated experiences.

  • Define the strategy: Set and defend a roadmap that balances relevance quality, coverage, and performance against clear business priorities.

  • Build evaluation and measurement: Stand up the metrics, benchmarks, and experimentation needed to know whether search is getting better, and to prove it.

  • Collaborate across teams: Partner closely with Knowledge Graph, SuperAnalyst / AI, Engineering, and Design so that search and the experiences built on top of it move together.

  • Lead and grow a team: Manage and mentor the curated-experiences / domain-expert PM, set clear ownership, and raise the bar for the search org as it grows.

  • Execute and deliver: Lead the end-to-end product lifecycle - from strategy and experimentation through launch, post-launch analysis, and iteration.

  • Clear Communicator: You can align engineering, design, and product marketing around a roadmap and gain buy-in to drive high-impact work.

  • Domain Experience a Plus: Direct experience in financial services, capital markets, or with our core customers (financial services, corporate strategy, consulting) is a plus, but not required.

Over 9,000 companies — from scrappy startups to global brands — use our platform to send billions of emails, push notifications, in-app messages, and SMS every day. Customer.io powers automated communication that people actually want to receive. We help teams send smarter, more relevant messages using real-time behavioral data.

About the role

Hi, my name is Diep Nguyen, VP Finance here at Customer.io, and I am looking for an Accounting Manager to partner with the Controller on our month-end close and serve as first-level reviewer for the accounting team. We're a global, remote-first, private company built on subscription and usage-based revenue, with a finance stack that includes NetSuite and FloQast, and we use AI throughout the business, including in Finance. Our accounting team covers revenue accounting, close, AP/AR, payroll, and treasury. You'll report to the Controller and work closely with partners in Sales, Legal, IT, People, and Engineering.

What we value

  • Ownership — You own a process from source data through the financial statements.
  • Curiosity — You keep asking why until you find the system behind the break.
  • A data-backed voice — You bring findings and recommendations to business owners with numbers behind them.
  • Practical AI use — You apply AI to speed up accounting work, with documented human review.

What you’ll do

  • Partner with the Controller on the monthly and quarterly close in FloQast, tracking deadlines and sign-offs, and help shorten the close through process improvements and AI.
  • Review and approve journal entries and reconciliations prepared by others on the accounting team, including cash, accounts receivable, prepaids, deferred commissions, fixed assets, accruals, deferred revenue, and payroll liabilities, and propose the bad debt reserve for Controller approval.
  • Draft the monthly flux analysis with root-cause explanations for material variances, assemble the close review folder, and support the Controller in the review with the VP Finance and CFO.
  • Assist the Senior Revenue Manager with revenue recognition (ASC 606), including deferred revenue, overage accruals, and usage true-ups.
  • Review AP, card, and payroll accruals and entries to confirm liabilities are recorded completely.
  • Prepare audit schedules for our external auditors and help document and test close controls with the Controller.
  • Coach the accountants who prepare the close, and apply AI tools to flux analysis, accrual review, and reconciliation matching with documented human review.

What we're looking for

  • 6+ years of progressive accounting experience, including at least 2 years reviewing the work of others or managing accountants
  • Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, or a related field
  • Hands-on month-end close experience at a SaaS company, including reviewing journal entries and reconciliations in an ERP such as NetSuite
  • Working knowledge of US GAAP for the accounts you will review, including accruals and unrecorded liabilities, prepaids, fixed assets, and payroll and commission liabilities, with specific knowledge of the allowance for credit losses (ASC 326), capitalized sales commissions (ASC 340-40), and the evaluation of errors and their materiality (ASC 250)
  • Experience supporting an external audit, including preparing schedules and responding to auditor requests
  • A specific example of using AI to make an accounting process or the close more efficient, which you built or deployed, and what it changed
  • Clear written and verbal communication with non-finance partners, and the judgment to know when to escalate to the Controller
  • Nice to have: CPA license (active or inactive) or a Big 4 or public accounting background; experience with NetSuite, FloQast, and usage-based billing; SOX or internal controls exposure; and remote-first company experience

Compensation & Benefits

We believe in transparency. Starting salary for this role is $105k–$122k USD (or equivalent in local currency) depending on experience and subject to market rate adjustment.

We know our people are what make us great, and we’re committed to taking great care of them. Our inclusive benefits package supports your well-being and growth, including 100% coverage of medical, dental, vision, mental health, and supplemental insurance premiums for you and your family. We also offer 16 weeks paid parental leave, unlimited PTO, stipends for remote work and wellness, a professional development budget, and more.

Clinical Trial Manager

Precision for Medicine is looking for an experienced Clinical Trial Manager to join our growing team. Candidates can work remotely in Hungary, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, UK or Spain.

Precision for Medicine is a precision medicine CRO. Precision’s uniquely integrated offering enables the science of precision medicine by combining novel clinical trial designs, industry-leading operational and medical experts, advanced biomarker and data analytics solutions, and an unequivocal real passion for rare diseases and oncology, in addition to working across other therapeutic areas.

You will be the hub of central intelligence for the studies you will be managing and will lead CRAs and oversee all clinical aspects of your study across multiple countries, ensuring timeline adherence and scope, whilst ensuring quality delivery. We encourage high-energy, dedicated professionals who enjoy a challenge, thrive in the details and flourish in dynamic environments to explore this opportunity.

We are addressing the challenges facing the research and development of novel compounds in Oncology and are dedicated to positively impacting the health and lives of patients around the world. If you take a consultative approach to trial management, proving to be a valuable partner in the trial operational delivery process, don't miss exploring working with us.

About You:

  • You love having responsibility and a say in how clinical trials are run
  • You plan ahead, but have alternative options and a flexible approach
  • You are client focused
  • You are well organised and able to manage timelines and shifting priorities, without sacrificing quality.
  • You communicate clearly, often and concisely and know that your role is crucial in keeping the trial running smoothly
  • You are a master at identifying any risks that threaten projects and handle them resolutely
  • You thrive and work with autonomy and ownership to deliver successful outcomes

The day-to-day role, and how we will support your continued growth:

  • Management and operational delivery of the clinical elements within a trial including site selection, start-up, enrolment management, site engagement and support, monitoring planning and execution, data cleaning activities and close-out
  • Successful execution of assigned trials and ensuring completion of trial deliverables
  • Ensure appropriate communication, regulatory documentation, and ongoing oversight of assigned trial(s) by working in close collaboration with other functional team members
  • Mentoring and training of team members
  • Identify challenges to study timelines/deliverables and offer creative action plans to the team/sponsor
  • Lead CRAs as they establish relationships with their sites for high quality oversight of monitoring, regulatory, IP, site payment and overall site correspondence activities

Qualifications:

Minimum Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education/experience in science or health-related field, including experience in the field of oncology

Other Required:

  • Demonstrable experience leading clinical aspects of your studies across multiple countries in a CRO / Pharma or Biotech company (in a dedicated 'clinical lead' role).
  • Significant clinical trial management experience in the area of oncology
  • Experience with CAR-T and Radiopharmaceuticals would be a strong plus
  • Working knowledge of GCP/ICH guidelines and the clinical development process
  • Availability for domestic and international travel including overnight stays

Skills:

  • Demonstrated computer skills (MS Office, MS Project, PowerPoint) and software experience (CTMS, eTMF, EDC, IXRS)

Competencies:

We combine deep science with deep data from advanced technological platforms, then layer on specialized expertise in the design and execution of targeted, adaptive clinical trials. Ultimately, we deliver robust insights that inform real-time decisions—and optimize the oncology development pathway.

The National Real Estate Practice Leader is responsible for advancing IMA’s national presence, growth, and expertise across the real estate industry. This leader brings deep knowledge of real estate risks, sophisticated carrier and market relationships, and a strategic mindset oriented around complex property portfolios, development activity, and evolving economic and regulatory conditions. The leader serves as a highly visible resource across geographies and builds a durable practice capability that markets, producers, service teams, and clients can use across IMA.

Essential Responsibilities:

Growth, Production & Market Impact

  • Drive national new business growth across priority real estate sectors, which may include multifamily, affordable housing, commercial office, industrial and logistics, retail, mixed-use, hospitality, development, and property management.
  • Actively support producers on complex real estate opportunities, including strategy, program structure, property and catastrophe risk, valuation, builder’s risk, casualty, environmental risk, cyber, management liability, claims, and alternative risk considerations.
  • Provide direct involvement on high-value pursuits, including complex portfolios, catastrophe-exposed assets, development projects, and organizations with sophisticated risk financing needs.

  • Build trusted relationships with real estate associations, centers of influence, lenders, capital partners, and other industry stakeholders.

  • Represent IMA in relevant real estate forums and bring emerging client needs, market changes, and partnership opportunities back into the organization.

Talent Development & Capability Building

  • Define the production, service, technical, analytics, claims, risk control, and leadership capabilities required for the practice to succeed.
  • Actively support specialty recruiting by identifying talent pools, target organizations, role profiles, and high-potential candidates, and by participating in interviews and selection.

  • Reduce reliance on any one individual or market by converting expertise into repeatable solutions, playbooks, tools, training, service standards, and delivery models.

  • Lead national practice calls and cross-market collaboration, promoting knowledge sharing and the transfer of proven approaches across IMA.
  • Partner with Marketing on focused thought leadership, events, association involvement, and market-facing content aligned with practice strategy.
  • Help markets replicate proven growth plays while adapting them to local asset classes, relationships, talent, and execution realities.

Performance, Accountability & Enterprise Leadership

  • Establish meaningful goals and expectations for growth, talent, capability, client value, activity, and execution.
  • Maintain a regular review cadence with market and enterprise stakeholders, surface risks and barriers early, and recommend adjustments based on evidence.
  • Create shared accountability across specialty, market, sales, and service leadership by clarifying ownership, milestones, resource needs, and decision points.
  • Represent the practice in enterprise planning and provide an objective view of opportunity, capacity, performance, and investment needs.
  • Measure success through the capability and results of the practice, not simply the individual activity of the Practice Leader.

Required Experience & Skills

  • Extensive real estate-related brokerage, underwriting, risk management, consulting, or adjacent experience, with strong technical knowledge of real estate exposures and insurance solutions.
  • Demonstrated credibility across relevant real estate sectors, client operating models, risk exposures, insurance markets, and competitive dynamics.
  • Experience supporting complex real estate portfolios, sophisticated placements, development projects, strategic pursuits, or industry-specific solutions.
  • Strong knowledge of property and catastrophe risk, valuation, builder’s risk, complex casualty, contractual risk transfer, claims, and alternative risk considerations.
  • Demonstrated ability to build senior-level relationships with real estate executives, clients, carrier leaders, associations, centers of influence, and strategic partners.
  • Proven ability to lead through influence across markets, functions, and reporting lines.
  • Experience recruiting, developing, mentoring, or deploying specialized talent.
  • Ability to convert technical knowledge into practical solutions, clear communication, scalable tools, and measurable growth or client value.

Competencies

  • Real Estate Industry and Business Acumen
  • Strategic Leadership and Commercial Judgment
  • Capability Building and Talent Development
  • Market Partnership and Growth Enablement
  • Relationship Building with Real Estate Executives, Carriers, and Industry Partners
  • Complex Client and Pursuit Leadership
  • Enterprise Collaboration and Shared Accountability
  • Effective Communication and Executive Presence
  • Execution Discipline and Follow-Through

jobs.title: National Account Director, Enterprise Access
jobs.description:
National Account Director, Enterprise Access

Company Overview

Immunome is a clinical-stage targeted oncology company committed to developing first-in-class and best-in-class targeted cancer therapies. We are advancing an innovative portfolio of therapeutics, supported by a leadership team with deep experience in the design, development, and commercialization of cutting-edge therapies, including antibody-drug conjugates. Our pipeline includes varegacestat, an investigational gamma secretase inhibitor for which an NDA has been accepted by the U.S. FDA; IM-1021, a clinical-stage ROR1 ADC; IM-1617, a clinical-stage solid tumor ADC; and IM-3050, a clinical-stage FAP-targeted radioligand therapy. We are also advancing a broad portfolio of early-stage ADCs pursuing undisclosed solid tumor targets.

Position Overview

Immunome is seeking a highly experienced and strategic National Account Director, Enterprise Access to lead integrated account strategy across a U.S. national footprint in support of our oncology portfolio. This role will build and sustain relationships with national and regional health plans, pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), and Key Account customer networks to advance launch readiness, appropriate coverage and reimbursement, formulary access, and therapeutic adoption following regulatory approval.

The successful candidate will bring deep expertise in payer access and institutional purchasing, recognizing the distinct operating models, decision processes, and account economics of each. This position combines direct account ownership, strategic negotiation, and executive relationship management with cross-functional leadership, serving as a primary resource for field teams and connecting headquarters strategy with local execution.

Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

  • Develop and execute multi-year Payer / PBM and Key Account institution plans with defined access objectives, stakeholder engagement, procurement strategies, and measures of success.
  • Apply commercial, Medicare Part D, and Medicaid expertise alongside community and integrated delivery network (IDN) business acumen, tailoring strategies to payer coverage decisions and provider purchasing structures.
  • Translate oncology market trends, clinical differentiation, reimbursement, and clinical pathway dynamics into national account priorities and commercial planning.

Payer Access and Stakeholder Management

  • Build executive-level relationships with pharmacy directors, medical directors, clinical leaders, and pharmacy and therapeutics (P&T) decision-makers across national and regional health plans and PBMs.
  • Navigate formulary and preferred drug list (PDL) development, utilization management, and coverage and reimbursement policies across commercial plans, Medicare Part D, and Medicaid fee-for-service (FFS) programs and managed care organizations (MCOs).
  • Map decision authority and payer affiliates; coordinate internal account teams to identify access barriers, align engagement, and advance appropriate coverage outcomes.

Institutional Access and Stakeholder Management

  • Build relationships with CEOs, CFOs, COOs, medical directors, pharmacists, and practice administrators across oncology customers and their member organizations.
  • Extend engagement to IDNs, health systems, hospital and community oncology networks, and national clinical pathway organizations, aligning corporate relationships with local customer needs.
  • Use approved clinical and economic evidence to support appropriate preferred formulary and pathway positioning with relevant provider and pathway decision-makers, respecting independent clinical decisions.

Strategic Negotiation

  • Lead payer, PBM, and community account strategy and negotiations, including pull-through opportunity, within approved authority; balance coverage and purchasing objectives, rebate commitments, pricing dynamics, and long-term business value.
  • Partner with Market Access, Finance, Legal, and Compliance to evaluate contract economics, 340B considerations, and Medicaid Best Price implications and secure approvals before commitments.
  • Prepare negotiation strategies for sophisticated counterparties, execute approved agreements, and coordinate implementation, performance monitoring, and renewals.
  • Translate local access and coverage landscape into coordinated field pull-through plans, with clear account responsibilities and adherence to company policies.

Value Communication and Market Intelligence

  • Partner with Medical Affairs and health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) colleagues to translate clinical and economic evidence into account-specific value narratives using approved materials and appropriate scientific support.
  • Tailor compliant communications to payer evidence needs, population priorities, and coverage considerations, and to Key Account, provider, and pathway stakeholders’ clinical and business priorities.
  • Monitor formularies, utilization management, coverage policies, clinical pathways, and oncology market developments; synthesize account insights and evidence gaps into actionable recommendations for internal teams.

Leadership and Collaboration

  • Serve as the primary payer and corporate accounts resource for field sales, connecting headquarters strategy, national agreements, and local execution.
  • Partner with Commercial field and Market Access colleagues on shared accounts, aligning priorities, responsibilities, customer messaging, and coordinated action plans; provide proactive consultation to Sales, Marketing, Medical Affairs, HEOR, Finance, Legal, and Policy.
  • Lead cross-functional account teams and mentor colleagues, fostering accountability, consensus building, and coordinated execution without relying on direct reporting authority.

Launch Planning and Execution

  • Lead payer and key institutional account launch readiness, aligning access strategies, contracting timelines, stakeholder engagement, and field execution with applicable regulatory approvals.
  • Develop and execute educational programs through all available channels with appropriate internal partners and review processes, maintaining separation between commercial and medical activities.
  • Tailor rare disease and rare oncology launch strategies to clinical differentiation and account needs rather than relying on approaches designed for large, high-volume therapeutic classes.

Qualifications

  • Significant biopharmaceutical market access or commercial experience managing national or major regional payer accounts and national oncology GPOs.
  • Experience across commercial, Medicare Part D, and Medicaid FFS and MCO markets, as well as community and IDN purchasing structures.
  • Proven account-planning success, senior stakeholder relationships, and appropriate coverage, formulary or pathway outcomes and field pull-through.
  • Experience leading payer, PBM, and oncology negotiations and evaluating pricing and contracting implications with Finance and Legal.
  • Experience communicating clinical and HEOR evidence with Medical Affairs support and developing educational programs through appropriate channels.
  • Demonstrated success working in a highly matrixed environment influencing cross-functional strategy, and coaching or mentoring colleagues.
  • Prior product-launch experience required, including account readiness and coordinated field execution.
  • Rare disease or rare oncology experience strongly preferred, with examples of account differentiation from large, high-volume therapeutic classes.
  • Ability to engage customers nationally; ability to travel up to 50%.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Deep knowledge of payer and PBM business models, revenues and incentives, and how insurance-side coverage differs from community and IDN purchasing.
  • Knowledge of formulary and PDL development, utilization management, reimbursement policies, and provider formulary and clinical pathway decisions.
  • Financial and contracting acumen across rebates, pricing, 340B, Medicaid Best Price, and key account economics.
  • Deep oncology therapeutic-area knowledge, including biologic and biosimilar access dynamics where relevant.
  • Ability to translate clinical and HEOR evidence into account-specific value narratives and identify evidence gaps with subject matter experts.
  • Executive presence, sound judgment, negotiation, stakeholder mapping, and relationship management skills across complex payer and provider accounts.
  • Cross-functional leadership and influence, including consultation, consensus building, mentoring, and collaboration across headquarters and field teams.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, strategic planning, and problem-solving skills; accountability and effective prioritization in a dynamic biotech environment.

Washington State Pay Range

$240,000—$269,908 USD

Join Our Experienced, Passionate Team

Working at Immunome gives you the opportunity to make a difference in the lives of cancer patients, contribute to developing best-in-class targeted cancer therapies, and work with some of the brightest and most experienced minds in antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) development.

Immunome’s office is charged with the collective excitement and passion of people working together to develop life-changing cancer medicines. Our team thrives in an innovative, collaborative environment where employees are empowered to do their best work.

Immunome also offers a comprehensive benefit program for you and your family, including:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage for employees and their dependents, including 100% company-paid medical premiums for employees
  • A 401(k) with employer match
  • Employer-paid life insurance, short- and long-term disability insurance, and AD&D
  • Paid time off, company holidays, and a week-long winter break between Christmas and New Years.
  • Paid parental leave

Immunome, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.
